article_title: Your bridal skincare guide for glowing, healthy skin before the wedding
sub_title: If you’re planning your wedding, start planning your skincare too. Here’s Dr Harshna Bijlani’s expert bridal skincare guide, month by month
article_content: You’ve probably curated moodboards, picked your palette and maybe even finalised your dream lehenga and chandbalis. But while the playlists and outfits fall into place, there’s one element that deserves equal attention: your skin. “Your bridal glow is not built in a day,” says Dr Harshna Bijlani, aesthetic physician, celebrity skin expert and founder of AgeLess Clinic. “It’s layered inside out with science, consistency and a little bit of soul care.” With six months to go, the focus is not just on looking flawless but on building a foundation that lasts, starting with lifestyle changes, skincare habits and treatments that work over time. A thoughtful bridal skincare routine begins here. This is the ideal moment to get serious about your skin prep. “The first step is always to fix your foundation, and I don’t mean makeup. I mean your lifestyle,” says Bijlani. She recommends consistent sleep (ideally by 11 pm), cutting back on sugar and dairy if you’re acne-prone, and using sunscreen daily. “Sunscreen is your skincare insurance policy. It protects your treatments, prevents pigmentation and keeps your glow intact.” Begin a personalised routine with actives like vitamin C for brightness, niacinamide to strengthen your barrier and retinoids (if suitable) for smoother texture. You can also start in-clinic treatments such as pigmentation correction through peels, Q-switch lasers or mesotherapy, and The three-month mark is peak treatment season. This window allows enough time for procedures that deliver long-term results but may need recovery. Energy-based options like Ultherapy, Fotona 4D or RF microneedling gradually lift and tone skin, with results appearing closer to the wedding. Regular IV drips containing glutathione, If you’re open to injectables, this is the right time for baby Botox to soften expression lines, subtle fillers for contour and hydration, and skin boosters for luminosity. “The three-month mark is when your skincare routine, workouts and diet need to go on autopilot,” says Bijlani. “Consistency now equals confidence later.” With a month left, avoid new products or aggressive treatments. “Your focus now is on maintenance, hydration and keeping inflammation down,” warns Bijlani. Skip first-time peels, strong actives or lasers. Stick to trusted facials such as hydra facials, LED light therapy and This final stretch is about calming the chaos. Stress and poor sleep can raise cortisol levels, leading to puffiness, dullness and breakouts. Bijlani recommends a simple routine: a gentle double cleanse, a hydrating serum with hyaluronic acid, peptides or ceramides, followed by SPF in the morning and a nourishing barrier cream at night. Cold water dunking can help tone and depuff, while The day before your wedding, give your skin a break. Avoid exfoliants, masks or new products. A gentle hydration mist, barrier cream and nourishing lip balm are enough. Stay away from waxing, shaving or picking at pimples. Use a cold compress if needed and focus on rest. A cup of On your wedding day, simplicity works best. Hydrate, then use only what your skin knows and loves–a mild cleanser, hydrating serum, moisturiser and SPF. Bijlani stresses the importance of at least one makeup trial, ideally a month before. “It’s not just about finalising your look. It’s about testing how your skin reacts to the products, especially base makeup and eyelash glue.” If you plan distinct looks for different events, schedule two separate trials. “More than two can confuse you more than help,” she adds. The calmest brides are always the most radiant. Don’t chase perfection. Focus on balance, breath and feeling beautiful in your own skin. Skincare doesn’t stop at your jawline. What’s on your plate matters as much as what’s in your products. Aim for 2.5 to 3 litres of water daily to keep skin plump and hydrated. Add antioxidant-rich vegetables like carrots, tomatoes and greens, and include Regular movement, breath work and proper sleep complete the picture. Trust the lasers and facials, but also trust the journalling, the tea, the deep breaths before bed. At the heart of every bridal skincare plan is calmness, the kind that no product can replicate.

article_title: A guide to bridal makeup for minimal brides
sub_title: Makeup can feel intimidating if you rarely wear it. Two experts share how to create a bridal look that feels effortless and true to you
article_content: For some women, makeup is second nature, the winged liner drawn with the ease of signing one’s name, a lipstick always rolling at the bottom of the handbag, a multi-step skincare-meets-makeup ritual that’s as natural as Then comes the wedding day, when every eye and every camera is on you. Makeup may be part of the day, but it should never make you feel like a stranger in your own Shradha Luthra, a bridal makeup artist, says it all begins with a conversation. “The most important thing to communicate is your comfort level. Tell your artist how much or how little makeup you usually wear. Even if that answer is ‘none’, it gives your artist a baseline. Share what makes you feel most like yourself, whether it is keeping your lips natural or avoiding anything heavy on the eyes. That is the starting point.” Eshwar Log, leading makeup artist, agrees. “Choosing the right makeup artist is everything. Look for someone skilled at skin work and minimal beauty. Have a meeting ahead of time to share your expectations for the wedding day and other events. Even sharing images of looks you do not want helps us understand your taste.” Both experts say skincare is the foundation. “A well-layered routine is key to achieving that glow from within,” says Log. Think lightweight ceramide moisturisers, brightening serums with Log suggests starting early. “Hydrate well, moisturise daily and use SPF. Simple steps that make any makeup sit beautifully on your skin.” The consultation or trial can help the non-makeup bride gain confidence. “It is about understanding each other’s energy,” says Log. “A trial of two looks—a skin-focused one and a subtle glam—helps the bride see how the makeup evolves over a few hours and how it holds up.” The most requested look for brides who rarely wear makeup is the elusive no-makeup makeup. Barely-there tint, soft blush, brushed-up brows and a coat of mascara. Luthra defines it as bridal makeup that feels invisible but is carefully crafted. “Evened-out skin tone, a natural flush, eyes defined just enough to look awake, and lips close to your natural shade—polished but never obvious.” Log adds, “Focus on enhancing one feature: skin, eyes or lips. If it is lips, pick shades that match your undertone, like peach or brown nudes, or a stain topped with gloss. Minimalism does not mean skipping steps. It means thoughtful choices that let the bride shine.” For brides who have never worn makeup, the process can feel daunting. “Explain each step, keep a mirror handy and let the bride see what each product does,” says Log. Music, at a comfortable volume, turns getting ready into a ritual. Luthra adds, “I start with the lightest touches—a hint of blush, sheer “Think of makeup not as a mask but as an enhancer,” says Luthra. After their paths crossed at a family wedding many years ago, Roshni and Jeel went their separate ways. We had the most splendid holiday there, lounging on a private boat, visiting villas, soaking in the Italian sun and creating one of the most unforgettable memories of our lives.” Wedding planning began soon after. Roshni was determined to make every event feel like a beautiful story brought to life. So, she enlisted the help of Hailey Shah of RHS Events to plan an elaborate four-day affair in Georgia, wonderfully captured for posterity by P.Taufiq Photography and his dream team. “The brief was that no two moments could look or feel the same. So, Hailey and I worked closely and came up with every detail from scratch.” Roshni says. Every moment felt honest and full of heart, just like we’d always imagined it to be.” concludes Roshni.

article_title: The bridal photography tips every bride needs on her wedding day
sub_title: From what to do with your hands to how to skip stiff poses, here is House on the Clouds founder, Siddharth Sharma's advice that will help you look and feel like yourself
article_content: The wedding décor will be dismantled and the So what do you do when the camera is everywhere, when you are battling humidity, high emotions and twelve-kilo embroidery, and are still expected to look flawless? We built a survival kit of bridal photography tips to help you navigate the day without awkwardness, or worse, your ‘resting stress face’ preserved forever in a high-resolution Google Drive. To do it, we teamed up with Siddharth Sharma, wedding photographer and founder of House on the Clouds, known for his dreamy, cinematic style. He has built a career coaxing nervous brides into looking effortlessly chic. For Sharma, it is not about the perfect angle or smile. His first rule is simple: stop performing. Sharma believes mimicry often dulls authenticity. “There’s no wrong way to be photographed, it’s your day, your personality, and that’s what truly matters,” he says. “The only time things feel off is when brides copy poses that they’ve seen online. That’s when photos can end up looking stiff or unlike you.” He adds that trusting your photographer helps create portraits that feel effortless and timeless: “The best thing is to let your own personality shine through while also trusting your photographer, they’re constantly observing you, your body language and your energy, and they know what will flatter you best.” Nerves show in the hands first. “Hands are sometimes a tricky part of posing but the secret is to give them something natural to do,” says Sharma. He suggests simple movements that feel like you: adjust your When you are juggling heels, emotions and missed calls, the lens can feel invasive. Sharma’s advice is to shift the focus back to the moment: “It is completely normal to feel camera-shy. A lot of brides aren’t used to being photographed this much. But the best way to look natural is to forget the camera sometimes and focus on the moment. Think of it less as posing and more as just being in the moment: small, genuine gestures photograph beautifully.” This mindset underpins his bridal photography tips throughout. Multiple outfit changes might sound exciting in theory, but they can quickly start to feel like a quick-change marathon. Between outfit changes, hair touch-ups and a rapidly ticking schedule, brides often feel like they’re caught in a wardrobe change montage. “The best way to Editing your schedule means you actually get to live in your outfits, not just change in and out of them. It’s better to slow down, savour each look, and give yourself space to enjoy the day. Should you go full Colgate or opt for a subtle Mona Lisa smirk? “The best kind of smile in photos is the one that feels natural to them. There isn’t a rule about showing teeth versus keeping it subtle. It’s more about what looks and feels authentic.”There’s no algorithm for this. You smile like you. That’s where the good photos live. The myth says the ideal bride knows every angle. Sharma disagrees. “The ideal bride is someone who trusts the team she’s hired. Once you’ve chosen your photographer, giving them creative freedom is the best gift you can offer. It makes the entire process flow effortlessly.” As he puts it, “It’s not that much about knowing how to pose or where to look, and more about being present, relaxed and open.” Bridal shoots are not fashion campaigns. Real emotion needs gentle direction. “Posing for models is very different from posing for What separates stiff from timeless often comes down to forgetting the camera. “The best moments happen when couples forget the camera and just enjoy each other,” Sharma says. “When you are present in the moment, the love and ease show up naturally.” Share a private joke, breathe, notice the flowers. The camera will find what is real. So, if anyone offers you cheese in the form of ‘say cheese,’ skip it. Stay real and let the camera catch you. With these bridal photography tips, your wedding album will read like a memory rather than a rehearsal.

article_title: This couple’s botanical wedding was a love letter to ritual, context, and modern grace
sub_title: Shradha and Nagarajan Chandrasekharan’s Bengaluru wedding was a gilded world of meaningful rituals, personal touches and botanical dreams, orchestrated by The Mogra Collective
article_content: Set against the backdrop of the scenic Nandi Hills, Shradha and Nagarajan Chandrasekharan tied the knot in their own special way. Theirs was more than just a union of two people. It was a celebration of their heritage, imbued with modern values. Complementing the heart of each ritual was a riot of colourful blooms and quaint personal touches that invited guests into their world. To put together their dream wedding, this Chennai and Bengaluru-based couple enlisted The Mogra Collective—a boutique event planning firm—renowned for their layered, luxury-focused and design-forward approach. The idea was simple yet profound: to honour their cultural roots while maintaining contemporary sensibilities. What followed was a series of five meticulously-planned events that felt truly personal and moreover, deeply theirs. The For their nuptials, they chose a neutral ritual that paid homage to both their backgrounds, without being shadowed by rigid patriarchal customs. Honouring the bride’s love for all things floral, the team at The Mogra Collective put together an extensive network of flowers around the The celebrations came to a close with a grand, twilight dinner held at Amita Rasa. A pale-green-and-earth-toned affair, the event sparkled with a 100-foot mirrored floor that reflected the hills and the stars. Inspired by Shradha’s sculptural Gaurav Gupta ensemble, this event was designed to exude luxury—a trademark of The Mogra Collective. Soft greens and muted earth tones of the floral palette were chosen to echo both the ensemble and the surrounding landscape. A memorable part of the decor, the 100-foot mirror served as a runway of light and movement. As the day melted into dusk, candlelight, stars, and a spectacular firework display shimmered across its surface. Every detail, from botanical urns to sculpted topiary forms, was calibrated to create a space that felt like a living installation. The five-course menu, curated by Chef Manu Chandra, was a true cherry on top. Spotlighting the couple’s travels and favourite flavours, it created an immersive experience for every guest—bringing them closer to Shradha and Nagarajan Chandrasekharan’s beautiful journey. Shradha, a children’s mental health professional with a passion for policy reform, lent her creative touch by designing her own outfits and rethinking all the stationery. Nagarajan Chandrasekharan, who leads a LiDAR-based technology firm, managed logistics with precision, turning spreadsheets into a quiet kind of art. Working as a team, they drew from each other’s strengths to ensure that their vision was brought to life. From hand-embroidered napkins depicting the couple’s pets to customised menus inspired by their favourite date spots, each element was chosen not to chase trends, but to hold meaning. The outfits, too, were a fitting mix of shimmering Kanjeevarams and elegant Sabyasachis, each with its own personal touch. As Karuna Reddy, founder of The Mogra Collective says, “We don’t design for spectacle. We design for feeling. For context. For story.” This philosophy is precisely why couples turn to them—to bring their stories and visions to life with honesty and authenticity. Every event is approached with precision and a keen eye for detail, making your big day a true reflection of your story—one where love always takes centre stage.

article_title: 26 engagement nails to try with celebrity inspiration
sub_title: From timeless neutrals to bold designs, these engagement nail ideas will have your ring finger ready for its close-up
article_content: Engagement nails are often minimalist–think French manicures or neutral shades–which makes sense in the era of Instagram announcement posts, with your ring finger hand on full display, says celebrity manicurist Tom Bachik, whose clientele includes Jennifer Lopez and Selena Gomez. But it's your special day (or, the run-up to your special day), so we say the rules are yours to make. Nail artist Brittney Boyce counts Olivia Rodrigo, Megan Fox and Kim Kardashian as regular clients, and she reports seeing more experimentation with colour and design. The best engagement nail, she says, is the one you love. “This all just comes down to personal style,” she says. For some, that's a short natural nail. For others, it's the Swarovski-encrusted nails JLo recently wore (scroll on for the inspiration, of course). So whether you’ve already found your forever person or are still using those crystals to attract him, her, or them into your life, it’s never too early to start brainstorming. Below are 27 engagement nail ideas to get those glam creative juices flowing. You’ll need this for when you book that nail salon appointment. A throwback to Margot Robbie's Oscar nails in 2021, manicurist Tom Bachik went with a natural shade. If you want length but don't have natural nails, try Apres Gel-X Extensions. When it comes to engagement manicures, neutral shades are foolproof—they match everything. This creamy tan acrylic will make any engagement ring stand out. But as with any mani, good grooming is essential. If you’re seeking a subtle design to elevate a bare base, opt for the classic French mani. Bachik painted thick white lines along the tips of Nicola Peltz Beckham’s long square nails for a dynamic look. We’re all about metallic sheens, but there’s something really warm about bronze. Choose this if you’re looking to put a unique spin on a basic bare or brown nail shade. Looking for some colour? Vibrant and alluring, Bachik’s cherry red nail look on Michelle Williams makes for the ideal engagement mani. Another subtle way to dress up any mani is with tiny nail art details, as seen here on JLo. We love Bachik’s addition of a small silver curve hugging the bottom of the French tip for an unexpected spin on a timeless look. More Jennifer Lopez inspo. This rich chocolate brown with grey undertones not only makes for a great neutral nail, but it also provides the perfect contrast to coloured engagement rings. Her green diamond just pops. It may seem too on-the-nose to wear white engagement nails before you get proposed to. But there’s no arguing that white nails make your engagement ring shine a tiny bit more. (Plus, there’s nothing wrong with expecting that ring; gotta manifest!). For just a hint of chrome, dress your French mani with textured silver tips. As a base, Boyce likes to use a milky neutral over something opaque and recommends something like the Aprés Nail’s Colour Extend Gel Bottle in Carla. Married lady Jennifer Lopez wore these Swarovski nails in her This modern take on a nail trend popular in the 1940s feels crisp and fresh—a bit of nail art, but nothing to distract from the main attraction. For something more unexpected and trendy, mix white and black streaks for a bolder engagement nail. Set these designs against a bare nail to ground the look. This super-shiny mani has a bit of edge in just the way we like it. Ethereal and romantic, milk bath nails evoke inviting calm and a sense of wanderlust (and they’re super-pretty). Blake Lively wears a creamy milk bath base with delicately placed floral decals that accentuate her ring. This Tiffany blue is a rich turquoise with a glossy sheen that will take your IG engagement photo to the next level. In true “quiet luxury” fashion, Sofia Richie Granger wears her natural short nails with her engagement ring. If you want to keep it bare but still polished, swipe on a clear coat like the OPI Brilliant High-Shine Top Coat, or the Dior Nail Glow Polish that gives you a hint of pink. Once upon a time, the black mani was reserved for Halloween and/or angsty teens. No longer: black nails are a modern classic, and one of the chicest options for an engagement nail look. Just take a cue from Kourtney Kardashian. Dark, edgy, yet still very much romantic—we’re here for it. If you’re still looking to get that glazed doughnut-inspired look, add some iridescent shine. Serena Williams goes for sparkly light pink nails that shine bright like her engagement ring. Ciara proves that mauve makes for a great go-to nail colour. The mix of purple and pink with cool undertones works for every skin tone. We love this warm gold-orange shade Beyoncé sports. It’s got sheer coverage and a light metallic sheen that doesn’t overpower the stunning ring on her finger. The creamy shade of this Essie pink polish (it's Bubble Away, a classic shade) is bold but still feels like a neutral. This is basically the red nail theory’s final boss (if you subscribe to that philosophy, of course). Celebrity nail artist Julie Kandalec credits one of her clients for the idea and describes it as “a deep brick-ish red with white chrome over it.” Striking yet chic, there’s nothing like a classic red to pair with your new ring. A look Kandalec recently did for Emily Blunt, this cool-toned champagne nail with silver French tips is an easy way to elevate a classic mani. (And we're loving the ever-popular almond-shaped nail that just elongates the fingers). Mixing two different shades in the same colour family can add some needed dimension and depth to your engagement nails. “Subtle, yet visually very interesting close up,” says Kandalec of the look. A two-toned nail is a classic (and easy to do, which is always a major plus). With its velvety feel and mesmerising shimmers, cat-eye nails are one of the most fun looks you can try—especially for an engagement mani. Either go all out with a full cat-eye or find a happy medium. Kandalec recommends a more subtle variation and suggests starting up top with the cat-eye effect before gradually transitioning it to a more neutral shade at the base. Looking for a deep infusion of colour? Kandalec says to go for jewel tones. “They’re rich in tone and luxurious,” she says. Her favourite is a cranberry red. But you can also opt for a deep emerald or purple to really make your engagement nails pop.

article_title: 16 best wedding destinations for brides who want their venue to match their personality
sub_title: Whether it’s a pristine sandbar in the middle of the Indian Ocean or a family-owned vineyard in the south of France—no matter how unconventional your tastes, we’ve found you a wedding destination to match
article_content: Can there be more to the best wedding destinations than just pretty backdrops to frame one of life’s biggest At this quaint sixth-century château hotel, you’ve got the glamour of the French Riviera but in a bucolic, secluded setting. Indulge in the French art de vivre with excursions to the Riviera, local markets and Provençal villages where you can tailor your celebrations with bespoke wine tastings and the best of gastronomy that the region has to offer. Sign up for a treatment at the award-winning Spa Saint-Martin by La Prairie, that can also be arranged in the hotel’s gardens under a flower-strewn cabana. This stately hotel overlooking the Arno river exudes an old-world charm, thanks in part to the fact that it is a Renaissance-era palace. Weddings here aren’t just opulent, they are also highly personalised—be it an afternoon tea ritual with your closest, a walking tour in the city guided by an art historian or events at venues with grand frescoes and gilded ceilings within the property. Ask the concierge team to put together a romantic dinner on the historic Ponte Vecchio bridge or set up a picnic at sunset for your family. Nestled inside 20 acres of gardens lined with olive and fruit trees, this palace hotel has hosted everyone from Alfred Hitchcock to Moroccan royalty in its century-long existence. There are grand salons in which to host parties and traditional Moroccan or Nhaza-style picnics and hammams to relax in with your bridesmaids. If you do somehow end up with time to spare, ask the concierge team to curate a visit to the local souks and medina, or an insider’s tour of the city on vintage motorcycles. This hotel might be contemporary in design but it is steeped in the cultural nuances of Kyoto. The an 800-year-old heritage pond garden at its heart forms the pièce de résistance for a tranquil wedding celebration. Culinary experiences are a big focus: the chefs can design custom menus for a relaxed welcome dinner or a farewell brunch. Thrill your guests with thoughtful, hands-on experiences—whether it’s a workshop in kintsugi (the Japanese art of mending ceramics with gold) or a quiet tea ceremony led by a local tea master. Framed by pine-clad mountain slopes, green meadows and snow-capped peaks, this 85-key boutique ski resort makes for an intimate escape with your closest—especially if food drives much of your relationship. Let the landscaped gardens and breathtaking views from the amphitheatre lawns act as the backdrop for your picture-perfect wedding, while you savour an authentic wazwan spread­—and then head to The Khyber Spa by L’Occitane to recover. For those interested in a tasteful wedding without too much flash and bang, this heritage family-run property offers the perfect mix of quiet charm and refined elegance, paired with bespoke dining destinations and renowned local boutiques and jewellery stores. Trust the team to tailor a wedding celebration after your heart, whether it’s a sit-down dinner for 100 guests featuring classic Rajasthani delicacies or a large meet-and-greet at the majestic Amarbagh ballroom. Everything about this 16th-century palace hotel, just 45 kms from Jaipur, speaks restrained glamour. It remains one of the finest examples of Indo-Saracenic architecture; its vintage charm preserved in hand-painted murals, bougainvillea-fringed courtyards and terrace gazebos. Sheesh Mahal is the crown jewel, featuring hundreds of hand-cut mirrors, jewel-toned glass work and delicate frescoes—an apt setting for that one big reception you want after a quick court wedding, ending in a spectacular display of fireworks. Is your wedding just an excuse to unwind in the midst of nature with your inner circle? Consider this boutique resort overlooking the backwaters of the Moira River. Here you’ll find a curated selection of rooms and villas with plunge pools—the perfect canvas for an intimate wedding where you’re surrounded by a forest and the sound of birdsong. The villa and poolside lawns make for a breezy setting for your nuptials and reception, while the Storii Lounge can host a a quiet welcome dinner or mehendi celebration. For adventure lovers, this boutique safari camp in Rajasthan’s leopard country offers unbridled luxury. With just 10 tented suites, the entire property can be your canvas for an intimate, unusual celebration—where guests can be treated to breakfast in the wild, sundowners by the lake, wildlife safaris, a walk with a Rabari herdsman and dinners in the company of folk musicians under starlit skies surrounded by the soft glow of thousands of lanterns. Imagine hosting your wedding at one of the largest natural islands in the UAE, where you get a vantage view of free-roaming wildlife. At this luxury resort, with just 30 pool villas overlooking the savannah (and gazelles grazing in the distance), host a cozy cocktail soiree in the wadi, enjoy a barbecue under the stars, say your vows at the beach at sunset and throw in a few safari experiences—life moves at its own pace here, promising a wedding unlike anywhere else. Set on the fringes of the Siswan forest, this sprawling resort with a striking traditional façade, serene gardens, fountains and reflection pools offers luxurious tented accommodation as well as rooms. Have your guests make the most of the tranquil beauty with guided treks and forest trails, raise a toast under the stars on the private poolside deck with glasses of bubbly and canapés and indulge in farm-to-fork dining and authentic Punjabi fare. Ask the concierge team to plan things for you—whether it’s sunset pheras overlooking the ocean, chartering a catamaran or paddle boarding with sea turtles. It could be the adventure of a lifetime. This 200-year-old fort turned boutique hotel boasts an impressive Jaipur gharana-style architecture—a great backdrop for your wedding. What’s more: the resort’s practices are rooted in sustainability, from the use of natural elements like local flowers, upcycled materials and earthen lamps in wedding decor, to encouraging guests to plant trees. Give your wedding party a sensorial experience with rooftop dinners, riverbed walks, village safaris and sunset high teas. This newly opened hotel, with its water conservation practices and use of live food counters instead of buffets to lower food wastage, is a perfect example of how luxury and sustainability can coexist. The spectacular Chand Baori, inspired by Rajasthan’s stepwells, would be great for your pheras; and there are several terraces to host a mehfil by moonlight. Spring for the Fairmont thaal experience—a feast showcasing lost Rajasthani recipes and heirloom cooking techniques. Designed as an homage to the sacred water palaces of Java, Jumeirah Bali is an elegant all-villa beach resort that captures the allure of island living. They prioritise seasonal menus, sustainably sourced produce, low-waste and plastic-free decor, compostable florals and supporting local artisans with guest-driven experiences like making Balinese ceremonial offerings and personalised Batik art. Couple that with luxurious accommodation and sweeping views of the ocean for a truly immersive experience. Weddings at this 19th-century manor—overlooking vine-covered terraces and the Douro river—are enhanced by their sustainable practices, such as the use of seasonal produce in their curated menus and upcycled materials in decor. Plan your nuptials under the shade of ancient olive trees in the garden, have your guests indulge in private wine tastings with local vintners or attend workshops in making their own cosmetics with local ingredients and essential oils—these memories will be etched in time.

article_title: 26 marriage tips to keep the spark alive long after ‘I do’
sub_title: The best weddings might be straight out of fairy tales, but the best marriages are fuelled by hard work, deep wells of patience and abundant empathy
article_content: The most enchanting weddings often feel like they’ve leapt straight out of a fairy tale, with glittering lights, tear-jerking vows and storybook romance. But once the confetti has run out and the cake has been eaten, the marriage that truly begins—a commitment that’s built on something far deeper. The strongest marriages demand hard work, the kind that shows up even when it’s inconvenient. Because while weddings may sparkle, it’s the quiet, consistent tending of love that makes a marriage last. Below, So you’re a double income household run by a power couple with soaring careers and sky-high ambitions? Between income-based power play, stealth overspending and a mismatch in financial values, “The sage Vatsayana wrote that for good sex, the genitals have to be fairly matching in size,” says mythologist and author of Begin by “sharing what family means to you from a space of understanding context, not from a space of blame,” suggests Mumbai-based psychotherapist Anusha Manjani. “In South Asia, we marry into networks of duty and history. Often what we call ‘interference’ by in-laws is unresolved enmeshment or unconscious loyalty. Partners are often trying to mature from fused roles like the ‘good child’, ‘dutiful son’, ‘obedient daughter-in-law’ and that can create conflict.” So what can you do about this? “Keep the focus on ‘we’—align as a team and be clear on what is okay and not okay when it comes to spending time with family. For example, how do we want to spend our holidays and festivals?” Come to this conversation not with rigid expectations, but patience while being firm and clear. “Think of this not as rebellion, but repair.” To begin with, says Mohan, pre-nups are not legally recognised in India and can get thrown out of court easily. And secondly, wouldn’t you rather enter a marriage, even one with a wealth imbalance, with openness and clarity? “This may be unsettling, but you’d rather do the hard work of tackling wealth planning early on,” says Mohan. “And if your partner or partner’s family is the one insisting on legalities, don’t be dismissive or look at it as an accusation. Try to understand what’s going on instead and consult your own lawyers on the whys and the whats. This is where you really get to know who you’re marrying, so don’t take this experience for granted.” Between endless tasks, a mountain of paperwork and a million Zoom calls (that could’ve been an email), it can be hard to take out time for each other when you’re both at work. Harder still when there’s an Instagram reel or Twitter storm always at hand to distract you. “Little updates during breaks like ‘I just ate’ or ‘having such a tough day’ can help you stay connected even when you’re apart,” says New Delhi-based psychologist Divija Bhasin. Memes or emoji work too, if those are your love language. Screens in bed and when we wake up—who are we really married to? “Create intentional screen free rituals,” says Manjani. “Ask them: what was especially joyful or challenging about your day?” It could be at a device-free dinner, while making a cup of coffee or reconnecting at the end of the day while doing chores. “It is not about the amount of time or money spent on dates but more about creating room for daily presence and connection with each other.” Anand recommends carving out 15 minutes at the end of every day for “very close, intimate, non sex time” and building it into your daily routine. “Lie down with each other naked and cuddle but don’t talk about sexy stuff. Talk about your day. The rule is, this does not lead to sex. This is to remind yourself how good and comforting and nice it feels to touch each other, to truly be with each other.” Of course, it isn’t fair that one partner becomes the default chef/maid/ house manager if the other is on a faster growth trajectory. “Sit down to ask: What does a functioning home look like to both of us? What tasks do we hate? What do we not mind? What can we afford to outsource so we don’t end up totally hating each other?” says Mohan. You can also draw up a joint chore schedule. “One person has late-night meetings on Tuesdays? Cool—maybe the other handles dinner that day and they swap on Friday. The idea is to be equitable (different from equal).” Maybe you’re so swamped with your partner track, you actually can’t do the laundry. “But then, perhaps you can handle all the bill payments or weekend grocery runs,” says Mohan. “The point is to demonstrate intent and to say, ‘I see this as our shared load and I want to carry my part’.” Anand suggests practising “relationship foreplay”. The key to good intimacy, she says, is transition: You have to be in the right frame of mind, not still thinking about that email you’re drafting or that contract you need to sign. She suggests watching a comedian together in bed (and naked, if you like) because “you can’t imagine what laughing together can do for your relationship.” Or the very tactile, sensory act of cooking. “Either you turn it into a game or it’s just a simple meal,” says Anand. “Think about the transitions that you actually use so it’s not like cooking with a friend.” “We all have core needs of being seen and heard, and listening with intention and attention is a big part of what is needed to build intimacy today,” says Manjani. A screen-less weekend can do wonders, she says: Stay in and read to each other or play strip Scrabble, go out and explore the city, but take time away from work and your screens. It can “ground, reconnect and bring more care to what the relationship needs”. Hit the padel court, go hiking once a week, ride the Peloton—whatever it is, make a habit of getting out of the house and into spaces where you can kick things up a notch, even allow your competitive side to come out and play. “Anything other than that mandatory weekly candlelight dinner date which comes with so much pressure to perform,” says Anand. They love going on road trips with their friends, you could spend the whole weekend knitting through re-runs of It’s never easy: An unexpected anxiety attack while getting ready for work or living under a black cloud for weeks. It’s not easy on them—or you. “But try to learn more about your partner’s mental health problems by reading about it,” says Bhasin. “We often tell people to be positive or be grateful to try and cheer them up but can end up invalidating their feelings in the process.” Instead, seek professional help but also understand that actually taking that help will be their call. “A long hug, holding their hand during a tough conversation, placing your palm gently on their back or leaning into each other can signal ‘I’m here with you, I care for you, I see you’ to your partner’s nervous system,” says Manjani. Maybe you don’t want sex after a harrowing week at work, but you do want… something. Set a 15-minute timer for judgement-free play, says Anand, and tell them to give you the neck massage or kisses on your stomach that you’ve been craving. Or, maybe you don’t like how they kiss you. Lack of courage, meet role-play. “A friend in the kink community came up with this wonderful idea,” says Anand, “try light sub and dom play. It’s like a verbal script where you basically issue directions. Plus, you can be sure that your partner is listening at this point because, I’m sorry to say, but a lot of the time they are not.” The reality of contemporary life is that we assess the world (and ourselves) in terms of productivity and can end up assigning value based on numbers. Manjani sees a lot of couples “keeping track of who did what or earned how much”. “It is important to use a shared language of respect and not comparison when talking about time and contribution. Try to name—and value the invisible labour and reclaim rest.” Sex toys, says Anand, are great to experiment with together because “they can help take the pressure off and then this time can just be for the sheer pleasure of being together. On days when you’re not up to it, it’s wonderful to have mutual masturbation.” And if all of that is too uncomfortable, then play with toys by yourself, she says, without the guilt. “The more you understand your body, the more you can guide your partner. It’s not their job to discover your pleasure points.” Maybe it’s real estate, or maybe it’s a joint retirement fund that you will sink into that round-the-world cruise you’ve dreamt of your whole life—but creating a long-term asset or goal together, says Mohan, is a powerful way of showing commitment. “You want to convey that the money you make is not ‘your’ money, but ‘our’ money. If you’re the earning or significantly higher earning partner, proactively include your partner in your financial decision-making process so he or she feels like you’re working towards a joint future.” Things change. You change. You might have realised you aren’t enjoying something you thought you were flexible about—or the opposite. Anand suggests having monthly talks about boundaries which, just like consent, is not a one-time thing set in stone—and this isn’t even restricted to sex. To make it a conversation, not confrontation, Anand and her partner would gather daisies on walks in the meadows behind their house, and then offer a daisy to each other for each new rule they wanted to set. “Create a ritual. It softens the edges.” Every once in a while, leave them a note noticing the everyday or unsaid gestures, says Manjani. Things like “thank you for always making me laugh at awkward family gatherings” or “thank you for making the reservations whenever we go out to eat.” They’ll love that you’re paying attention. Think you might be bisexual? Want to try cuckolding? “Don’t go try it and then come back and say, I enjoyed that,” says Anand. “You have to remember that marriage is like a contract that you sign. There are certain unwritten rules and the main one of monogamy is fidelity.” Talk about it with your partner, she says—you might be surprised at just how willing they are to go along with it. If you or your partner want to try polyamory or an open marriage, Anand’s advice is to look up the subject to understand what questions need to be asked. “It’s not as simple as deciding that one wants to also sleep with somebody else at the same time. There are some basic questions you need to deal with that don’t even fall in the emotional paradigm—things like STIs, living arrangements, financial arrangements, legal repercussions. Remember: this requires even higher levels of trust than being monogamous.” Maybe it’s not even Tinder; maybe they’re just talking—to ChatGPT. “Even though AI can become a proxy for unmet needs, the actual work is in facing what those needs are—was it emotional availability, curiosity, lack of judgement or distraction? Is it a symptom of loneliness or disconnection, or is one partner trying to reclaim something they have lost—desire, aliveness or validation? In therapy, we don’t rush to close or repair the relationship but create space to understand these needs and check if it is possible to reconnect and repair,” says Manjani. “Create time to check in with the other,” says Manjani. “Ask: do you need Comfort (need for support and rest), Connection (time to spend together, affection, touch) or Celebration (need to be appreciated or to celebrate a small win)?” And then follow through with action, however small. On one side is rhythm and habit (or worst case, total monotony). On the other is discovery and reconnection. “Try new things: dance or doodle, introduce your favourite childhood games and activities to each other,” suggests Manjani. “Find ways to create joy—because that joy is glue.

article_title: A Rajkot wedding inspired by travel, heritage, and a touch of retro glam
sub_title: Naiya and Sidd Chhayani’s wedding had strong Gujarati influences alongside picturesque backdrops and 1920s elegance
article_content: Their first date in Boston unfolded without pretence—two creative spirits talking about travel, culture, food, and their shared love for dogs. That conversation marked the beginning of a relationship shaped by curiosity and connection. Over the next two years, Naiya and Sidd explored the world together, turning travel dreams into shared memories and strengthening their bond with every adventure. It was there that they decided their story would return to Rajkot, Gujarat, where love, heritage, and artistry would converge in a wedding captured by Planning a wedding across continents required the couple to make multiple trips to India. From selecting the floral arrangements and curating exquisite menus to working directly with artisans, every decision was guided by their vision. The process, though meticulous, was filled with joy. Their advice to other couples: “Enjoy the process and don’t get lost in the details. Communicate, set realistic expectations, and remember it’s about celebrating your love.” The festivities began at Regency Lagoon Resort, Rajkot. The mehndi ceremony, enhanced with green accents and tropical arrangements, echoed the couple’s love for cultural detail. The following day, the haldi and sangeet unfolded with a Greek-inspired aesthetic—blue and sunlit yellow elements setting a festive tone. Guests embraced the colour palette, while the couple stood out in striking pink tie-dye. By nightfall, the sangeet transformed into a Bollywood-inspired celebration, complete with custom posters, a red-carpet entrance, a Filmfare-style frame, and spirited performances from friends and family. The wedding ceremony itself was envisioned as a balance of tradition and contemporary design. A pastel palette, accented with peach, softened the grandeur, while floral installations, reminiscent of Singapore’s Gardens by the Bay, evoked the couple’s shared passion for travel. The groom, dressed in regal attire with a sharply tailored ivory sherwani paired with a white turban and a ceremonial sword, channelled a maharaja-inspired ensemble. His arrival began in a vintage Rolls-Royce before he mounted a white horse for the final stretch, accompanied by dhol, a live DJ, and dancing. The bride wore a crimson lehenga, embroidered with zari and resham. Her look was completed by traditional jewellery and a Sabyasachi mangalsutra with a lion motif—an auspicious symbol of strength and prosperity in Gujarati culture. While the ceremony was steeped in tradition, the couple introduced intimate Western elements: handwritten vows and the bride walking down the aisle with a white bouquet in hand. The reception shifted into a world of retro glamour. Black-and-gold decor, sweeping gowns, and tuxedos set the tone for a celebration reminiscent of the Great Gatsby era. Champagne toasts and high-energy performances by the newlyweds and their loved ones brought the festivities to a dazzling close—a fitting finale to a wedding that honoured both heritage and modernity. For those who will be journeying down the aisle, the couple reminds them to delegate when needed so they can be fully present for their special day—something they credit to the artistry of

article_title: Vogue’s A to Z wedding directory will fully prep you for your special day
sub_title: The one-size-fits-all kind of wedding is a thing of the past. Let this A-Z directory be your guide for crafting a celebration that is authentic to you
article_content: The era of cookie-cutter weddings is over. Today, it’s all about creating a celebration that feels like it was designed for you from start to finish. Whether you’re dreaming of an intimate garden soirée or a three-day destination spectacle, the possibilities are as limitless as your imagination. To help you navigate it all, we’ve put together an A to Z wedding directory covering everything that injects personality into your nuptials. Think of it as your blueprint for a wedding that is equal parts stylish, personal and unforgettable. From handwoven textiles to locally-sourced seasonal Bachelorette trips are trading late nights for early mornings: think sunrise Pilates and sound baths. Unwind with barre classes and post-class matcha at MAJA Canggu, Bali, SHA Wellness Clinic, Spain or The Farm at San Benito in the Philippines. Cold feet? Stick them in a From saffron crème brûlée to mini gulab jamun cheesecake, Sage & Saffron by Aditi Dugar, Single Thread by Manu Chandra and Gaia Gourmet by Shilarna Vaze create vertitable edible art installations where Indian classics meet global favourites. Save paper (and your sanity)—digital invites are eco-friendly, elegant and will spare you the stress of awkward small talk when visiting relatives. Posh Invites by Gauri Agrawal and The Murphy Studio take away your logistical troubles by designing personalised wedding invitations. Roses and hydrangeas for a touch of romance; marigolds and jasmine for a traditional aesthetic; tulips and ranunculus for minimalists—trust Weddings by Gurleen M Puri and Interflora India to design your dream wedding space. Deep-cleansing facials to signature shaves, self-care for men has levelled up. Grooms can turn to Truefitt & Hill for luxury barbering or indulge in treatments like a Korean hair spa and face gym at Florian Hurel Hair Couture & Spa. No bridal trousseau is truly complete without at least one heritage weave. A Banarasi silk or a rich Kanjeevaram, passed down through generations, carries stories woven into every thread. Invest in an heirloom from Advaya, Tilfi or Ekaya. The infrared sauna penetrates deep into the skin to flush out toxins, soothe muscles and promote blood circulation. Sign up for a quick session at The Wellness Co. in Delhi, Salt World in Bengaluru or Reaviva Holistic Health in Mumbai. The technical artistry involved in the making of a piece of jadau jewellery—uncut diamonds, precious stones and pearls set in gold—gives it the stature of art. Tyaani, Jaipur Gems and The House of MBJ have you covered. The humble kolhapuris were the subject of much debate recently after they walked onto the Prada runway, but there’s no question about their comfort value. Designers like Aprajita Toor, The Sole Sisters and Sandalwali reimagine them for the wedding wardrobe: think zari, mirrorwork and pearl embellishments. A few days before the big day, sign up for this miracle treatment that can sculpt the face and reduce water retention at the Quan Spa, JW Marriott Mumbai, Kaya Kalp Spa, ITC Maurya New Delhi or Jiva Spa, Taj West End Bengaluru. From high-octane sangeet nights to a sundowner mehendi, mirrorwork is the playful alternative to an otherwise zardozi-heavy wedding wardrobe. Find your piece at Arpita Mehta, Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla or JJ Valaya. Add a pop-up manicure station to your mehendi festivities to queue up for some fun. Nail Rituals in Delhi, Studio Nails by Anisha Mulchandani in Mumbai and Nailbox in Bengaluru bring glamour and polish straight to your venue. In the intricate art of fragrance layering, oud is that versatile element that pairs well with vanilla, sandalwood and more. Luxury fragrance houses like Maison Francis Kurkdjian and Ajmal Perfumes are known for their refined takes on oud—elegant, addictive and as timeless as your vows. Does an intimate pre-ceremony to exchange vows and inside jokes without a crowd watching sound nice? Take a good photographer along—the folks at House On The Clouds, Joseph Radhik or The Wedding Filmer—to capture the moment. Rose quartz’s association with healing, love and emotional clarity makes it a befitting beauty companion to keep close in the lead-up to your wedding—especially for a glow that goes beyond skin-deep. RAS Luxury Oils and Dromen & Co offer beautifully crafted rose quartz facial tools. Pastels and neutral hues may often take centre stage, but rani pink’s unmistakable vibrance guarantees it a spot in a bride’s trousseau, like that fun cousin in your bridesquad. Find your bold fashion moment for the sangeet at Frontier Raas or House of Masaba. Kokum-urrak spritzers for a summer soirées, toddy-based nightcaps for winter sangeets: Master mixologists like Yangdup Lama and Pankaj Balachandran can keep things lush with potions highlighting Indian brands and local ingredients. Sculptural centrepieces, softly glowing taper candles, place settings in elegant calligraphy: The tablescape is emerging as the canvas to tell a visual story of togetherness. Designers like Altair by Janki Desai and Eeshaan Kashyap specialise in crafting immersive experiences—styling food, cocktails, tableware and decor to create cohesive and memorable sit-down dinners. If you’re looking to recreate that timeless Mughal charm through your bridal jewellery, look no further than uncut diamonds—or polki. Jaipur-based Raniwala 1881, Hazoorilal Legacy and Indriya by Aditya Birla can help you find the right pieces that carry the perfect balance of craftsmanship and modern elegance. There’s something about the Indianised bridal veil—lightweight tulle with intricate embroidery—that elevates your whole bridal look like little else. Designers like Sabyasachi, Gaurav Gupta and Falguni Shane Peacock know how to balance tradition with wearability. Whether it’s a quiet affair or a 700-person spectacle on your vision board, pulling it off needs a seasoned planner—like Devika Narain (known for detail-rich weddings) or Motwane Entertainment & Weddings (who can whip up larger-than-life productions). For that secret element that can take your wedding to a whole other level, craft a signature scent together—one that captures your story and lives on in memory. Brands like Jo Malone and Maison 21G offer bespoke fragrance experiences where you can co-create a scent to wear, gift or even diffuse throughout your celebration. After all the madness of wedding planning, unwind and recharge with a short yoga retreat at Dharana at Shillim or Ananda in the Himalayas—nothing like a weekend of vinyasa flows, gut-cleansing meals and natural quietude to reenergise you before the big show. Astrology likely played a role early in your relationship to help you spot red flags—so why leave the zodiac factor out of your big day? From Fizzy Goblet’s zodiac sandal heels and Mrinalini Chandra’s customised kaliras to Outhouse Jewellery’s celestial-inspired pieces, the stars truly align in the last alphabet of this wedding directory.

article_title: Janhvi Kapoor’s dream wedding reflects a new era of intimate celebrity unions
sub_title: Across India and beyond, celebrities are stepping away from grand productions for ceremonies that feel private, personal and true to them
article_content: When Janhvi Kapoor talks about her dream wedding, concepts like drone shots, elephant processions and endless pre-functions aren’t in the frame. In her It’s not about capability—Kapoor could command a stadium if she chose—but about intent. What she desires is an intimate ritual, not a production. “I know I want to get married in Tirupati. I definitely don’t want too many people there. I want it to be quick and I want the honeymoon to be very long,” she tells us. And she’s not alone. Across industries and time zones, stars are turning away from maximalist “all eyes on me” weddings in favour of something private, spiritual and stripped back. Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth tied the knot this year in a 400-year-old Telangana temple, announcing it with a single set of photographs. Alia Bhatt and Ranbir Kapoor married at The mood extends beyond India. Charli XCX married musician George Daniel at Hackney Town Hall in London with 20 close guests, in a Vivienne Westwood The draw of the big fat celebrity wedding hasn’t disappeared. But in an age of constant exposure—when even an airport look gets dissected–the wedding is the one moment stars want wholly for themselves. Kapoor’s generation in particular sees resonance in what feels genuine, not staged. That shift shows up in clothes, too. Kapoor imagines herself in a Manish Malhotra creation but wants something familiar and comfortable. Alia Bhatt wore an This doesn’t mean extravagance is dead. But the definition of “dreamy” has widened. For Janhvi Kapoor, it’s vows at Tirupati and the freedom of comfort. For others, it’s a balcony, a farmhouse or a restaurant. What’s appealing now is not scale but sincerity. So in the absence of any need to prove anything to the world, what’s left is the privilege of being present with oneself, your partner and those who truly matter. Isn’t that what marriage is about, anyway?

article_title: Two fine jewellery ateliers that are reimagining Indian heritage
sub_title: From rare gemstones and distinctive design to a hundred years of legacy craftsmanship, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels and Mehta & Sons create bespoke creations that tell stories across generations
article_content: Jewellery is a reflection of the wearer. The necklace you pick to wear on a special day to the simple studs that adorn your ears on the daily—every trinket you choose tells your story. Two distinguished jewellery brands, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels and Mehta & Sons, celebrate this individuality with their pieces—the unique cuts, gemstones and designs ensuring that there is something for every discerning customer. Scroll further to know more about the two brands, their design sensibilities, their founders and more. Since its inception in 2005, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels has become synonymous with intricate craftsmanship, rare gemstones, and distinctive design. From heirloom classics to contemporary statements, each jewel is brought to life using a curated palette of the world’s finest treasures—Golconda diamonds, Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies, Basra pearls, Kashmir sapphires, Paraiba tourmalines, and Baltic amber, set in 18K and 22K gold, often finished with unique polishes and textures. The founder, Dr. Anjali Bhimrajka’s journey into fine jewellery was shaped by artistic instinct and passion. With academic accolades including a Ph.D. in Alternative Medicine, Dr. Bhimrajka is a true polymath. She turned her childhood fascination into a lifelong calling, taking herself to the Gemological Institute of America, where she trained in jewellery design and diamond grading—formally setting the foundation for her namesake label. Every jewel at Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels begins with ethically sourced diamonds and gemstones—selected not only for their brilliance, but for their integrity. Age-old techniques are not just preserved—they are reinterpreted through a modern lens, creating designs that feel timeless yet distinctly contemporary. Their latest collection, Rêve Parisien is an ode to the romance of Paris. It translates the charm of a bygone era into radiant elegance and modern sophistication.The collection introduces neckpieces, ear pendants, and rings with vibrant coloured and uncut diamonds, enhanced by blue sapphires and tanzanites—highlighted by mandarin garnets and colourful sapphires. For a hundred years, Mehta & Sons has been more than a jeweller—it has been a custodian of tradition, artistry, and trust. An ancestral house built on values passed down through generations, the brand remains deeply rooted, humble, and true to its heritage, even as it evolves to meet the aspirations of the modern world. Mehta & Sons began its journey almost a hundred years ago, in 1931, and to this day, every piece at the atelier brings with it this legacy of craftsmanship and quality. Carrying forward his ancestral heritage, Mr. Narendra Mehta has shaped Mehta & Sons into one of India’s most trusted names in fine jewellery. A man of vision and quiet strength, he believes that every creation must reflect not only artistry but also soul. For him, a jewel is more than design—it is emotion, value, and legacy, to be cherished by generations. His philosophy ensures that every piece leaving the atelier carries with it the same integrity and devotion that has defined the brand for a century. The artisans of Mehta & Sons honour tradition while embracing innovation. Known for their intricate gold-work, mastery in diamond settings, and the rare art of blending vibrant gemstones with precision, the house has perfected its craft over a century. Each jewel reflects the devotion of both artisan and founder—where craftsmanship is not just skill, but an inheritance. To mark its centenary, Mehta & Sons unveil their latest collections, Strata and Eterna—paying homage to their legacy while embracing modern luxury. The bridal line captures the grandeur and sentiment of Indian tradition, crafted as heirlooms of love. The collections feature diamond creations elevated with rare gemstones, exuding bold elegance and timeless charm. Both these brands are a celebration of heritage—tested by time, yet created for today. They aim to bridge the legacy of Indian heritage with a global sensibility, crafting modern heirlooms that transcend trends and generations.

article_title: 9 bridal makeup products that belong in every wedding day kit
sub_title: Call it your bridal toolkit for everything from toasts to tears
article_content: Some brides wouldn't dream of their ideal beauty look without enlisting the help of a We have curated a ready reckoner with the key makeup products in any kit along with tips on how to use them, so that you're well prepared for your big day. When you get down to brass tacks, Without proper prep, your skin can be something of a blotched nightmare. After all, you’ll want your makeup to hold up through the last selfie, toast and twirl. This makes primer extremely essential. The thumb rule is to use a You probably won’t get enough shut-eye during your wedding festivities, but this is the one time when you want to look your fresh-faced best. This requires a seriously heavy-duty A Lock in your base with a pressed or loose setting powder. One swipe of a brush will absorb excess oils to give a visibly flawless finish. A compact size will also be handy for touch-ups later. Your wedding day is the perfect opportunity to pack some punch with your eye makeup. Look for a palette that combines neutrals and metallic shades. Warm, earthy tones work best with Indian skin. Shades of gold, bronze and copper also do well together, and the modern Indian bride can opt for these colours without a second thought. A waterproof formula is the only answer to smudge-proof, sweat-proof and even tear-proof your eye makeup. Make sure to add a highly pigmented long-wear eyeliner to your makeup kit. A highlighter can serve as the perfect pick-me-up for your complexion, and provide a lit-from-within glow when applied to the high points of the face (cheekbones, tip of the nose, brow bones, and Cupid’s bow). Choose your formula according to the look you want to achieve—a powder highlighter will give you a matte look, a cream or balm version will leave you with dewy face, while a liquid highlighter will provide the most intense colour pay-off. The last step to your bridal makeup, lipstick is a staple. Keep a red, pink and a nude at the ready. While matte formulas will last the longest, don’t have any qualms about opting for a creamy option.

sub_title: Jasmin Parikh and Hiren Babaria’s wedding highlighted their Indian heritage and unfolded over various cities in the US
article_content: There’s something special about tying the knot at a place that is replete with history and tradition. For this couple, it was Naples—a favourite from one of their weekend getaways in Florida encouraged by her parents ‘Sunday Fundays’ tradition. It was only fitting then, that Jasmin Parikh and Hiren Babaria, chose to have their wedding at the newly renovated  Ritz-Carlton Naples in Florida. The venue’s quiet sophistication was the ideal backdrop, featuring swaying palms and turquoise waters, an amalgamation of tranquility and celebration. Quiet, joyful and endearing, Jasmin and Hiren's love story was the kind that revelled in a slower pace, unfolding gently over multiple dates. It started off with a message sent by Jasmin with the help of her aunt, and a reply from Hiren days later while he was on a trip to Hawaii. And then the conversations began, and translated to dates. Their first date in Dallas was cinematic, thoughtful and the connection was natural and instant. They had sushi at Uchi, spent time taking long walks in the rain, and cute gestures like holding an umbrella over her head had Jasmin convinced this could lead to more. Jasmin is from New Jersey and Florida, and Hiren is from Dallas. Their long-distance relationship certainly drove up airline ticket sales with the couple taking over 30 trips between cities like New York, Chicago, Orlando and Dallas. The proposal on a secluded beach in Oahu was much like their relationship, quiet and a celebration of their love. Jasmin had an inkling and got her nails done and got them matching outfits, a girl can never be too prepared. As they walked onto the beach during sunset hour, feeling the sand on their toes, Jasmin saw the flowers and the “Will You Marry Me” sign. Jasmin describes the feeling as surreal and although Hiren was fairly certain about the answer, he wanted to make a meaningful yet grand gesture. The celebrations began with an intimate welcome dinner at The Ritz-Carlton Naples. The property, which was recently renovated, provided the perfect backdrop with everything looking brand new. The couple’s interests found translation in the decor, food and the personalised details. The menu, curated by chef Satish, had a mix of traditional Gujarati dishes and international staples like sushi, incorporating all the flavours the couple loved. The following morning, the couple had the traditional Grah Shanti, a ritual to mark an auspicious beginning of the celebrations. This was followed by the Haldi ceremony where the couple was showered with turmeric and petals, with laughter and joy filling the air. The couple then took a dip in the ocean with their friends and family cheering them on. This sentiment was captured beautifully by P.Taufiq Photography. Sangeet night saw enthusiastic performances by friends and family, and a dance floor that was buzzing into the early morning with Foram Shah at the console. It ended with garba, a nod to their roots. The wedding ceremony had the couple promising each other a lifetime of love and happiness under a lush floral mandap, and in the background, the sound of waves and swaying palms. With that,  Ritz-Carlton Naples hosted a big Indian wedding, planned by Bharati Shah, Electric Karma International and supported ably by the floral decor work of Utopian events. The band, a favourite with the guests and the couple alike, and at the console was Empire Entertainment. Serenading the guests with melodies on her violin was Amy Serrano. A nod to her roots, the bride wore Tarun Tahiliani for the sangeet, wedding, and reception. She wore a custom Mani Jassal outfit for welcome night, and a custom-designed Haldi outfit by the bride’s sister. The groom wore Siddesh Chauhan for the welcome night. He wore a Tarun Tahiliani outfit for the sangeet, and his sherwani for the wedding was by Shyamal & Bhumika. He wore a soft pista green gently complementing the bride’s pink bridal lehenga. For the reception, he wore a deep maroon tuxedo to contrast with the bride’s ivory outfit. All of this was captured beautifully by PTaufiq Photography. Brought together by chance, this love story was etched in the memory of everyone who attended, and certainly made a case for finding love in the unlikeliest of places.

article_title: Expressions of joy
sub_title: Izzhaar, a gifting solutions brand is turning emotions into mementos for you and your loved ones
article_content: Finding the right gift that conveys the love, regard and care you have for someone can be a herculean task. Be it an anniversary, a wedding, or a festival—special moments like these deserve to be commemorated with thoughtful gifts. Taking the onus of giving your emotions a tangible form is Izzhaar, a brand born in 2014, that promises to make gifting emotional and intentional. Founded by Ruchita Bansal, a designer with a deep love for thoughtful aesthetics, Izzhaar began with one goal: to craft gifts and invitations that speak the language of the heart. Bansal’s brainchild wasn’t born because the world needed another gifting brand—it was because the founder thought that something was amiss. Izzhaar wanted to capture that feeling when a gift lights up someone's eyes, not because of how much it was worth, but because of its meaning. What started as a passion project soon evolved into a thriving business—one where every design is a reflection of affection, culture, and connection. Offering value for money gifting solutions, Izzhaar is known for its bespoke wedding hampers, artisanal invitations, home décor, and festive hampers. The brand offers exclusive options to their customers—be it a pastel-toned invitation inspired by a couple’s journey, or a sustainable hamper to reward hard-working employees; no two pieces are ever the same, because no two stories are the same. At the heart of it all is Bansal’s creative vision—guided by soul, not trend. “Luxury gifting isn’t about grandeur. It’s about care, connection, and meaning. We don't create to impress, we create to express,” she says. Izzhaar collaborates with artisans who believe in slow, impactful creation and are meticulous about the small details. The brand cares deeply about the planet, creating consciously with sustainable materials and focusing on pieces that become lasting keepsakes, not disposable gestures. With sustainability at its core and curated creativity in every detail, Izzhaar continues to create an impact in the modern Indian gifting scene.

article_title: This bride's classic red vision came alive with a Sabyasachi lehenga for her California wedding
sub_title: Dr Jasmine Singh's lehenga was hand-stitched and embroidered with traditional gold and silver threads, while the borders of her two veils featured handmade kiran fringing in hand-beaten gold and copper
article_content: For many brides, their wedding day is a unique opportunity to honour their heritage, often through fashion. Such was the case for Indian-American bride Dr Jasmine Singh, a psychiatrist based in California. “Even as a child, I knew – without a doubt – that no matter who I married, or when I married, I would have a Sikh wedding ceremony, and I would wear a traditional red Indian lehenga with gold embroidery,” she explains. “My mother has countless photos of me as a little girl dressed in a tiny red lehenga, adorned with a gold mathapatti and haathphool, and proudly wearing a bold red lip.” When the time came for Jasmine to curate her own wedding day looks for her marriage to Dr Sandeep Mann, she knew immediately that she wanted to work with Indian designers, especially on a red lehenga – that instantly recognisable Indian bridal outfit. “It mattered to me that my wedding outfit was made by hands and minds that understood the symbolism embedded in every motif and stitch,” she explains. “I wanted to wear something that wasn’t just beautiful, but meaningful; something that connected me to my culture and heritage.” Having become familiar with his work decades earlier, Jasmine immediately thought of turning to the celebrated Indian designer Sabyasachi (who memorably dressed Priyanka Chopra for her wedding celebrations) for her lehenga and jewellery. “I first heard about him when I was a student at UC San Diego,” she explains. “I remember being captivated by the news that an Indian designer had shown at Milan Fashion Week. Since then I’ve followed his career, watching him dress countless brides – including many of India’s most celebrated actresses.” Jasmine started by selecting her wedding day jewellery from Sabyasachi, while she went back and forth on which of his red lehenga to wear and how to customise it to suit her bridal vision – often having two-hour long video calls with his team in India. “The first piece I selected was the necklace, followed by the earrings and then the bangles – my mother insisted I include Sabyasachi polki bangles,” she says. “Then came the custom mathapatti, nath, and haathphool. Somewhere in between, I found myself gravitating towards a floral motif lehenga from the Red Collection in the Heritage series. I waited before making a final decision, wanting to be certain. Shortly after meeting Sabyasachi in person during a visit to Los Angeles, I knew it was the one.” The mathapatti was inspired by one of Sabyasachi’s first famous brides, the actress Anushka Sharma – though she wanted hers to feature South Sea pearls, to match the rest of her look. “I was told by the Sabyasachi jewellery director that any changes such as this would have to be approved by Sabyasachi Mukherjee himself,” she explains. “I was delighted when I learned that he had signed off on the changes. The piece was also custom made to the measurements of my head, which I thought was a great attention to detail, as it was custom-fitted to frame my face perfectly from ear to ear.” Indeed, Sabyasachi as a rule does not allow customisation, so it was up to Jasmine to convince him of her vision for the lehenga too. “After explaining my reasoning, some customisation was allowed,” she shares. “I discussed with him that I wanted my second veil for my head to be different from the first that would be wrapped around my body, so that it could add more visual interest, which they agreed to.” One particularly special touch was the floral motif on the skirt – a brand new design. “It resonated with me on a personal level – my name is Jasmine, after all – and it beautifully complemented the wedding’s setting,” she explains. “Alongside my production team, we built a custom structure on my family’s estate, nestled within the estate’s gardens, and centred our design concept around an enchanted garden of wildflowers. This lehenga echoed that vision perfectly, and wearing it felt like stepping into a dream I had helped create.” The Sabyasachi team also crafted a custom silk organza palla for the ceremony, finished with gold sequins and a tilla thread border. “In Sikh tradition, the groom wears the palla, which is handed to the bride by her father – symbolising the start of the couple’s spiritual journey,” explains Jasmine. “Sabyasachi graciously completed this bespoke piece in record time, and it arrived just days before the wedding. I was later told it had only been made once before – for the actress Katrina Kaif – making it all the more meaningful.” Unsurprisingly, a lot of craftwork went into Jasmine’s lehenga, which was hand-stitched and embroidered with traditional gold and silver threads, while the borders of her two veils featured handmade kiran fringing in hand-beaten gold and copper. “My lehenga arrived in California a few weeks before the wedding,” recalls Jasmine. “The first time I wore it was late at night, with my mother by my side. I slipped it on – it fit like a glove – and when I saw myself in the full-length mirror, I cried. I was on the phone with Sabena, the head of Sabyasachi, and she was deeply moved by my reaction. In that moment, it truly felt like my vision and dream had come to life.” With so much love and detail going into the look, it’s unsurprising that Jasmine intends to wear the pieces again. “I believe fashion should be both enjoyed in the present and preserved for future generations,” she says. “And I don’t think preservation should come at the cost of fully experiencing the joy of wearing something now.” For her, the entire process was a pinch-me moment. “I see myself as someone who embodies two cultures: born and raised in the United States, yet deeply in touch with my Indian heritage,” she says. “That duality, what I call biculturalism, can sometimes bring difficulties with identity and with managing the two opposing cultures, but sometimes the juxtaposition can be beautiful, and that is something I find in Sabyasachi’s designs: a rare and beautiful balance.”

article_title: Is your boyfriend planning a beach proposal? He needs to read this
sub_title: Learn everything to know about planning a perfect beach proposal, from tips on selecting a location to how to make a rain plan
article_content: A beach proposal is a favourite for a reason. The calm crashing of the waves, the feeling of your toes in the sand and the spectacular backdrop of the ocean sky at sunrise or sunset are a dreamy combination to craft the perfect romantic moment. Indians, especially, love beach proposals because they have all the makings of a Ahead, see all the proposal planning tips you’ll need to kick off your beach engagement. Choosing the right beach location is key to guaranteeing a beautiful proposal setting. First, consider the destination that feels right for the engagement. Is there a beach you often frequent together? It could be special to revisit this place in your romantic history for your proposal. Planning a beach vacation? Scout out the best beaches for proposals near your destination with a beautiful lookout, or seek a more private cove. If you are less familiar with the area, you might want to check online for frequented spots or ask your hotel concierge for any tips. If you’re staying at a resort, they may even have a special area on the property that can be the perfect location for your big moment. As you likely don’t want hundreds of spectators around that can take up prime sand real estate, it’s important to decide on a not-so-busy time to get down on one knee. Consider hitting the beach in the off-season when there aren’t as many sunbathers about or at an hour when the location is relatively empty, like when most people are at dinner. You can even plan a romantic picnic on the beach during this hour before you pop the question. It’s also important to consider the best ambience based on the time of day: not when the sun is too bright, but definitely when it’s just at the horizon. Not only will it be beautiful to watch (and give you an excuse to get your S.O. out there for the surprise), but the light will be wonderful for photos. Helpful hint: Bring a sweater or extra blanket in case the temperatures drop when the sun is no longer in sight. As I am well aware, bad weather can easily throw a wrench in your proposal plans. In my case, a windy forecast made my plans for a post-engagement dinner on the beach a less-than-ideal situation. So, we had to change the location for the second act of the proposal just hours prior. No matter your situation, it’s always important to have a rain contingency plan. Especially if you have hired a photographer or pre-planned a celebration afterwards, you may need to find another covered spot to pop the question. Always have a backup in place when you are first scouting out your ideal beach locale. Deciding on the right outfit for your proposal is a tricky task. On the one hand, you don’t want to give away the surprise by showing up overdressed for a beach day. But, you also probably want to look more polished than usual, especially if you’re documenting the proposal. Try to find a happy medium or create an excuse for a slightly Another important factor of your ensemble is that it needs a spot to hide a ring box. A jacket with an inner pocket, spacious pant pockets, or a bag can be key to keeping your surprise hidden away. Just be sure your hiding place is secure so you don’t leave the ring on the beach. While you will always have the memory of your proposal, it’s also fun to have images or videos of the special moment to come back to and share with your loved ones. One of the best solutions is to find a local photographer to document the moment as it happens. This can lead to a great photoshoot with you, your new fiancé and that engagement ring you spent months picking out. If you don’t want to hire a pro, you could also task a friend or family member to do the job with an iPhone. Just be sure they can stay hidden so as to not give away the surprise and are a trusted hand with tech. Once your partner (hopefully) says yes, it’s time for you both to celebrate. Don’t just plan the proposal itself. It’s a great idea to also have plans in place to take in the moment, whether in an intimate atmosphere or with your closest circle. A bottle of bubbly and a beach picnic can be the perfect way to enjoy your newly engaged bliss. Or, you can make a reservation at a nearby restaurant for a more polished toast. Some to-be-weds like to kick off their engagement era with a bang and invite friends and family for a surprise engagement party. Just be sure you’ve had previous talks of engagement and know it’s a done deal before you have anyone fly out for the festivities.
