article_title: A Czech bride, a Telugu groom and an Indian baraat in Prague
sub_title: Two cultures, two venues and one unforgettable celebration. Here’s how event and wedding planning company, RVR Eventz & Design and RVR PRO meticulously crafted a wedding day for this couple, across continents and traditions
article_content: In a world saturated with left swipes, fleeting connections and catfishing stories, Karolina Ebel, a lawyer-turned-entrepreneur, and Chaitanya Aluru, an engineer, found the kind of love written about in fairytales. It was a rainy day in New York, and a thoughtful connection over a dating app that sparked this love story. Barely a month into the relationship, Karolina knew that this was the man she was meant to marry. There was no grand moment, no epiphany, just quiet certainty. At a cliffside near Carmel-by-the-Sea, California, Chaitanya surprised Karolina with a wedding proposal, two weeks before their formal engagement. Saying ‘yes’ at her favourite spot with Chaitanya’s handwritten note hidden inside a bouquet of roses was surreal. It was this note that Karolina kept close to her heart, embroidering it on her wedding veil with words that read: The couple commemorated their union with a three-day wedding in Prague, Czech Republic, complete with an Indian When it came to choosing a wedding destination, Prague held a special place for the couple. It was Karolina’s hometown, and a place they had visited together on a vacation early in their relationship. For them, the city’s old-world charm, connection to the bride’s roots, and stark contrast to their fast-paced Silicon Valley life made it the perfect location. Chaitanya, who holds his Indian heritage and family traditions close, envisioned incorporating a traditional Hindu wedding. The couple’s shared vision for their wedding was to honour both cultures, blending vibrant Indian rituals within a European setting. To bring this vision to life, they chose the experienced team at RVR Eventz & Design. The couple hosted two ceremonies across iconic venues in Prague—an Indian wedding at the Mandarin Oriental and a civil ceremony and reception at the grand baroque Chateau Troja. The Indian wedding festivities began with an outdoor traditional The Czech civil ceremony, by contrast, was a formal legal celebration officiated by a registrar, followed by a reception with European flair, filled with food, drinks and dancing. One of the most unforgettable moments of the wedding was when the Locals and tourists paused to pull out their phones, capturing what felt like a movie scene unfolding in real life. Chaitanya, in a traditional sherwani, led the procession with friends and family dancing joyfully behind him. The air was filled with laughter, flower petals and the infectious rhythm of celebration. This wasn’t just a wedding tradition; it was a joyful moment of cultural fusion. Planning a wedding that spanned continents and cultures came with its fair share of challenges. Much of the wedding décor, bridal wear, and ceremonial items were shipped from India via air cargo. Several vendors and team members had to navigate visa approvals, and Prague’s rainy weather threw a curveball the day before the outdoor ceremony. “This was one of the toughest weddings I’ve planned,” says Priya Maganti, CEO at RVR Eventz & Design. “Planning a wedding in a new country is always a challenge, but every country I’ve worked in before had already seen Indian weddings, and they knew what to expect. Prague was different.” From explaining rituals to helping guests embrace cross-cultural customs, the team handled every detail with care. “The concept of an Indian wedding was new to many of the Czech vendors and guests, but now there is a growing appreciation and understanding of what it involves,” Maganti adds. Guests on both sides leaned in to celebrate each other’s cultures, whether it was through clothing, food, or participating in rituals. Czech guests wore lehengas and saris for the Hindu ceremony, while Indian guests donned elegant Western formals for the civil wedding. In a whirlwind of legal permits, hand-embroidered veils, tailor-made blazers, and a multi-cuisine menu, RVR Eventz & Design and RVR PRO ensured that every element of the couple’s vision came to life with authenticity and heart.

article_title: Sweet treats for the big moments
sub_title: The Laddoo Wala is making weddings special with sweets that are rooted in tradition and made with a modern hand
article_content: Weddings today are more than just ceremonies. They are expressions of identity, story, and emotion. The Laddoo Wala, an Indian mithai and savoury brand, honours this shift by reimagining the role of mithai in modern celebrations. The brand has set out to redefine the way Indian sweets are experienced—not as festive afterthoughts, but as elevated essentials. TLW focuses on clean ingredients, refined flavours, and thoughtful presentation. Their laddoos are hand-rolled in small batches with less to no sugar, using alternative sweeteners like jaggery and dates and with no added colours or preservatives. The result is a sweet that feels both nostalgic, healthy and refreshingly new. But TLW isn’t just about laddoos. Their growing repertoire includes silky barfi blocks, crisp savoury blends, and seasonal offerings that bring variety and versatility to any moment of celebration. Each product is developed with a strong attention to detail, balancing indulgence with today’s evolving preferences. With options that are gluten and cholesterol free, and naturally sweetened, there is something for everyone. The brand’s approach extends beyond taste. At TLW, design is an integral part of the experience. Their packaging is thoughtful, with embossed boxes that evoke warmth and nostalgia, and trays that become part of your home. Each wrap, label, and note is crafted with care, often carrying a little story inside—adding another layer of meaning to the gift. What truly sets TLW apart is the emotion embedded in every bite. Some connect with the richness of the motichoor, others with the gooey texture of their Every wedding the brand is a part of is approached as a creative collaboration. Whether it’s bridesmaid proposals, mehendi favours, or welcome hampers, they work closely with families and couples to co-create something truly exclusive. This year, they’ve expanded their repertoire with playful yet elegant additions like the ‘Laddoo Pops’ and ‘Savour Me’s’, a fresh take on the traditional laddoos and savouries that are perfect to share, to travel with, and for interactive displays. They carry craft and flavour with a touch of whimsy—designed for the contemporary celebration. Alongside this, the brand’s bespoke trays, savoury tins, and new barfi block formats bring depth and variety to your wedding table, all while staying rooted in Indian flavour profiles. At TLW, it’s the small things that make a wedding unforgettable, the welcome box that feels like a hug, the flavour that sparks a childhood memory, the handwritten message inside a hamper that makes someone pause. The brand believes in thoughtfulness and in creating mithai experiences that are as meaningful as the moment they belong to.

article_title: From Pichwai to Zardozi: Crafting a wedding of meaning and elegance
sub_title: What began as a chance encounter turned into a tale of culinary adventures, thoughtful gestures and shared calm—culminating in a deeply personal wedding at Raffles, Udaipur
article_content: They say matches are made in heaven, and perhaps that’s true, but matches are also made over shared plates of food. As they say, the way to one’s heart is through the stomach, after all. Sidharth Sharma, a restaurateur and owner of several renowned hospitality ventures across New York and New Jersey, knew this all too well. Sharma met Dhara Patel, a physician assistant, also from New Jersey, at a friend’s birthday in the Poconos, and it didn’t feel like they were meeting for the first time—there was a quiet familiarity, discussions about food they enjoyed, and shared experiences about growing up Indian-American. “For our first date, I took Dhara on a romantic picnic,” reminisced Sharma. After many personalised food tours and candle-lit conversations through the years and around the world, he popped the question in Napa Valley, surrounded by beautiful vineyards—recreating their first picnic date. “That first date stayed with me—the excitement, the ease, the joy of it all. When he recreated it in Napa to propose, it took me right back to that feeling. Saying yes wasn’t even a question—it was the easiest, happiest answer of my life,” Patel gushed. A dreamy wedding followed, rooted in the couple’s approach to love—grounded, enduring, and filled with genuine joy. The celebration of love took place across three days at Raffles Udaipur, a lakeside property known for its European-meets-Indian architecture and quiet luxury. The wedding was an homage to the couple’s cultural roots, and every detail was artfully preserved by P.Taufiq Photography—the team that captured both the grand entries and the quiet, in-between moments that depict a love story. The festivities opened with a spirited welcome lunch spread across Raffles Udaipur and Taj Lake Palace, where guests were greeted by the pulse of dhols, the melodies of Rajasthani folk musicians, and vibrant cultural performances—Kachchi Ghodi dancers, flutists, Raavan Hatta artists, and Matka performers. While welcoming their guests, the bride’s mehendi—crafted by Jayshree Panchal—became a conversation of its own, adorned with Pichwai cows, Ganeshji, peacocks, elephants, and swans, weaving together symbols of grace, good fortune, and devotion. This set the tone for a weekend of thoughtful detail and joyful celebration, both high on emotion and aesthetically unforgettable. The Mehendi and Sangeet took over the Great Park, transitioning from tropical Rajasthani day motifs—florals, birdcages, and pops of colour—to a twilight fantasy of chandeliers and lush floral canopies. The bride wore a custom Mayyur Girotra lehenga embroidered with a menagerie of birds and elephants for the Mehendi and a custom StudioSush floral blouse, later transforming into a shimmering gold StudioSush lehenga paired with a Rahul Mishra blouse for the Sangeet. “All of my looks were thoughtfully assembled by Style by Susmita. She brought my vision to life through carefully coordinated outfits, custom-designed jewelry, and beautiful hair and makeup,” said Patel. The groom matched her energy in color-coordinated daytime wear and a custom PourLui look for the Sangeet. The second day began with Haldi. Held at the poolside, it was a riot of laughter, turmeric, and sunlight. Mughal-inspired, vibrant floral decor was the backdrop as friends and family playfully applied haldi while showering the couple with rose petals and love. The Varmala ceremony followed. It unfolded beneath ‘The Promise Tree’—a towering floral sculpture symbolising growth and commitment. The wedding ceremony took place indoors, under a mirrored aisle and a floral mandap conceptualised as a ‘Mirror of Forever’. Lagnageet artists, led by Darshana Gandhi, lent a soulful backdrop to the pheras. Simultaneously, guests rang bells during the pheras, infusing the ritual with a collective sense of sentimentality. As the pheras concluded, guests gathered around the couple, walking them out in a moment of shared joy and intimacy, only to be surprised by a display of fireworks that lit up the night sky. article_title: Sparkling through generations: Jewellery that endures

article_content: Bridal couture plays a pivotal role in the grandeur of an Indian wedding, where fashion is as much a spectacle as the ceremonies themselves. Bridal outfits are representative of tradition, status, and personal taste, with designers translating cultural heritage into couture statements. Rare Heritage, a brand under the Mehta Emporium umbrella, was founded to add value to the country’s bespoke bridal jewellery. Starting out as a specialized bridal couture hub in 2014, the brand has now transformed into a premier fine jewellery house. The expansive 5,000 sq. ft. Mumbai atelier is both a creative sanctuary and an experiential showroom, making it the go-to destination for India's brides. Built on compelling paradoxes—premium yet approachable, selective but inclusive, it offers something for everyone, from understated minimalists to bold statement-makers. Rare Heritage has been a part of high-profile celebrations in the country while being endorsed by celebrities like Sonam Kapoor and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Every design is driven by a narrative, transforming individual pieces into legacy treasures meant to be passed down through generations. The brand’s insights into today’s bride offers a glimpse into the ask—pieces that are contemporary and yet timeless. Rare Heritage crafts collections that maintain relevance across decades. Each piece embodies cultural heritage, blending ancestral techniques with fresh perspectives to create deeply personal connections that extend far beyond ornamental value. The brand’s three directors, Manushi Singh, Nakshatra and Varun Mehta lead with vision. Singh’s design philosophy revolves around creating enduring relevance—pieces that feel modern yet possess the power to outlive fleeting trends. Her sophisticated aesthetic sensibility and forward-thinking approach have established the brand's authoritative presence in India's luxury jewellery landscape. As Singh brings timeless modernity to the forefront, Nakshatra infuses the brand’s creations with deep emotional resonance. Nakshatra champions jewelry's capacity to stir profound emotions and create lasting memories. His design methodology focuses on generating that transformative moment—when a bride connects deeply with a piece, creating bonds that extend well beyond the wedding day. Mehta’s perspective seals the deal, as he ensures that every design is mindful of the legacy it carries. He views each design as a chapter in an ongoing cultural narrative, often spanning multiple generations. His commitment centers on preserving ancestral wisdom within contemporary frameworks, ensuring every piece honours its roots while embracing evolution. “Every bride who walks into our atelier shows us something new about the power of jewellery. There’s always this moment—you can see it—when she finds a piece that feels like it belongs to her. That’s when it stops being an accessory and becomes a memory, a legacy. We’re not just making beautiful things; we’re creating keepsakes for life’s most meaningful chapters. The true test isn’t how well something shines in photos—it’s whether her daughter will one day wear it and feel that same pull. We always return to this truth: emotion is timeless. When it’s real, it never goes out of style.” Says Singh. Rare Heritage is set to launch its upcoming collections, Rare Beyond the Borders and Rare Love, two collections that draw from the brand’s deep archival legacy while also looking to the future.

article_title: Twelve years, one weekend, and a lifetime of love

article_content: Some love stories unravel with such quiet inevitability, it's as if they were always meant to be. Bride Akesha Sanjay and groom Aakash Thakor grew up just minutes apart from each other in South Florida, yet, like every romantic meet-cute, their story only began the summer before senior year of high school. “Looking back, it’s funny to think how many times our paths must have crossed—sharing mutual friends, going to the same community events, probably even standing in the same rooms,” Akesha mentions. They met at a Miami Heat NBA Finals watch party; Akesha, as always, was locked in—cheering, yelling at the screen—when Aakash noticed her, amused but intrigued. Little did they know that this was just the beginning of their forever. They quickly became high-school sweethearts—what started as a teenage friendship turned into a lifelong bond, one that endured distance, time zones, and countless changing careers. “Despite the miles, we always found our way back to each other,” they share. Fast forward to 12 years later, Aakash proposed to Akesha at sunset in Cabo, and the rest, like they say, is history. “I had a feeling it was coming—after so many years together, you kind of just know. But nothing could’ve prepared me for how beautiful and thoughtful it was. He had reserved a private stretch of beach at a gorgeous resort and planned an intimate dinner just for the two of us. The sun was setting, the ocean was in front of us—it was a moment I’ll never forget,” Akesha exclaims. So, when it came to their wedding, they knew it had to be a celebration of their story—a blend of grand gestures surrounded by their closest family and friends and a little bit of ‘Florida’ in all the celebrations to honour the city where it all began. Set against the Waldorf Astoria Riviera Maya, the backdrop was perfect. “It allowed us to have our dream sunset wedding and offered a variety of venues for each event, making every celebration feel unique and closer to our Floridian roots,” adds the bride. PTaufiq Photography captured the nuances of every smile, sentiment, and hidden undertone in pictures preserved for life. And there was ample to be captured, for each event boasted a different theme. The couple teamed up with Mala Events to bring their dream wedding weekend to life, curating every detail with intention and heart. Once the venue was secured, their vision truly took shape. The celebrations kicked off with a joyful joint Haldi ceremony, setting the tone for a weekend full of colour and culture. The welcome party channelled their shared love for Mexican cuisine, Latin music, and laid-back Florida vibes. The Saatak ceremony was a seamless blend of Indian tradition and modern design exemplified by Akesha’s ombré pink Manish Malhotra lehenga, a piece that “combined classic craftsmanship with contemporary flair”, she adds. The couple exchanged vows at sunset, with the beach as their breathtaking backdrop. Akesha wore a stunning Sabyasachi lehenga paired with a delicate Christian veil, while Aakash complemented her look in a regal Tarun Tahiliani sherwani. “It was the perfect expression of who we are—rooted in tradition, but shaped by a modern worldview,” she shares. The Sangeet pulsed with the vibrant energy of Miami—think neon colours, palm trees, and dancing late into the night. That was followed by a sleek black-tie reception, combining elegance and modern flair with glowing candles, cascading chandeliers, and the bride’s bold Gaurav Gupta gown stealing the spotlight. A surprise performance by British singer-songwriter Jay Sean, blending American and Indian hits that had all the guests on their feet. While DJ Sharad of DJ USA curated an electrifying set that kept the energy high and the dance floor packed all night long. Prashe Decor transformed each venue into a reflection of the couple’s cultures and personalities—seamlessly blending vibrant florals with refined, elegant elements. Musaafer, helmed by Michelin-starred Chef Mayank Istwal and his team, curated an unforgettable culinary journey, masterfully balancing traditional flavours with modern flair. Choosing PTaufiq was effortless; Aakash and Akesha had long admired their work. PTaufiq Photography captured every heartfelt moment in both photo and film, preserving the joy, love, and magic of every moment. Surrounded by their closest family and friends, the couple’s wedding was truly a heartwarming reminder of love transcending boundaries.

article_title: 17 unique engagement party ideas for every type of couple
sub_title: An engagement party is a fun way to start your celebrations on a high note and bring together friends and family who might join you along your wedding journey
article_content: Whether you’re planning a proposal or recently said ‘yes,’ you might be brainstorming engagement party ideas to kick off your Ahead, we round up unique engagement party ideas to help you get inspired for your own pre-nuptial fête. From cocktail parties to fun activities, see a few ways to make the most of your engagement season. No need to wait a few weeks or months to celebrate your engagement. If you’re planning a proposal (and are 100% sure your partner will accept), consider following up getting down on one knee with a surprise Rather than Who doesn’t love a good poolside bash? Guests can take a dip, soak up the sun and lounge by the water. A theme is always fun: opt for a tropical aesthetic, complete with crowd-pleasing margaritas and piña coladas. Keep things refreshing with boozy popsicles as a sweet treat, and don’t forget to have some baskets around stocked with sun essentials—think sunscreen, pool towels and sunglasses. The “I do” BBQ is a classic engagement party idea, and one that requires minimal party planning for the couple who prefers a laid-back yet tasteful affair. Ideal for the spring and summer seasons, it’s also easy to tailor to your surroundings, be it an indoor grill, communal rooftop or a full backyard setup. For cocktails, keep it simple with spiked lemonade pitchers and a well-stocked beer tub. Don’t forget the ice and the vegetarian options to balance out the burgers and hot dogs. Add a personal touch with a signature BBQ sauce, French fry bar or a make-your-own ice cream station. You can check out Pinterest for further inspiration. Halloween isn’t the only time of year you can dress up—and a costume party can also serve as the perfect front for a surprise engagement announcement if you’ve kept it under wraps. If going for full-on costumes isn’t your style, a subtle engagement party theme can be just as lively. Perhaps, a throwback to a Roaring Twenties speakeasy, complete with Champagne towers, a live jazz band and a list of Prohibition-inspired signature cocktails. If you feel like donning ’70s threads, a roller disco might be just the groovy ticket; or, for an air of mystery and opulence, a murder mystery masquerade. If you’re a pair of film buffs, host a movie night for your entourage. Transform your abode into a home cinema by renting a projector and popcorn machine. You could also make it a pyjama-themed party and encourage your guests to come in comfy PJs. Whether you opt for an indoor theatre or a snug, outdoor setup, the ambience is key. Enhance the cosy feel with plush blankets, a wide selection of beverages and, of course, movie theatre candy. Choose an all-time classic or romcom for the main feature, or showcase your own collection of cherished home videos and photos for that extra personal touch. It’s the perfect excuse to be cheesy, after all. A late-morning affair is a particularly chic idea for your engagement party, Whether in your own backyard or a local park, a picnic is a wholesome get-together for the low-maintenance couple. Craft a delectable cheese board, adorned with a selection of charcuterie, sandwiches and lemonade for beverages. Skip the live band; grab your speaker and set the mood with your specially curated Spotify playlist. To accommodate any dietary restrictions, encourage guests to contribute their favourite finger foods. You can even embrace a Parisian-themed picnic, with an array of fruits and jams, well-paired wines and madeleines. Or, transport your luncheon to the sun-kissed charm of Positano with a refreshing Caprese salad, Aperol spritzes and bougainvillaea centrepieces—and don’t forget the limoncello digestif. (However, A cocktail party proves that glamour need not strain your budget, favouring light bites over a full-course meal. Hire a mixologist to craft a signature cocktail inspired by the happy couple. The bartender could also offer a cocktail-making class, and guests can leave with a personal cocktail-making set as a party favour. Also, you can’t go wrong with a live band. For a close-knit group of friends, rent out a cabin or a couple of glamping tents for a weekend retreat. A grown-up take on summer camp, you can hike along scenic trails during the day, and when the sun sets, gather around the bonfire to swap nostalgic stories while roasting marshmallows and eating s’mores. For the newly engaged couple seeking an elevated experience, indulge in a wine-tasting escapade with picturesque views. (For beer drinkers, a brewery promises an equally enjoyable outing.) Depending on where you live, you can arrange for a tour bus or an organised winery trail for a day of vineyard hopping. And, should you prefer the comfort of your home, simply hire a sommelier for a private wine-tasting session. Just don’t forget the hors d’oeuvres and cheese. Hit the deck with your fiancé and your favourite crew for a boat engagement party. Planning this event is as easy as chartering a boat in a nearby marina for a fun celebration on the water. Be sure to make sure guests can enjoy sips and nibbles by bringing on catering or hiring an on-board staff to keep the cruise in high spirits. Whether you love an intimate concert or a night out dancing, hiring live musicians for your engagement party can absolutely step up your celebration. Take time to find the right artists that can set the tone of your event and have them fill your party venue with the perfect soundtrack for your festivities. Since a wedding is a joining of two families, why not get your two sides better acquainted by making your engagement party a family reunion? Bring everyone together, either at your own home or a fun destination, where you can make introductions and create closer bonds between your extended family members. Another perk of this style of event? Everyone will be a little friendlier by the time they hit the dance floor at your wedding or sit around the table at future holiday dinners. Want your guests to do more than just mix and mingle over food? Why not make your engagement party a special carnival night where they can play games, win prizes and enjoy nostalgic fair treats? To bring this idea to life, you could DIY game booths or even bring in large carnival rentals to transform an outdoor space into the perfect summer night celebration. Crashing waves, crackling fire and a sunset over the horizon are the perfect recipe for a great beachside engagement party. Either book a private event space at a beachside restaurant or get a permit to put together your own celebration that has a coastal flair. Get engaged in the winter? Take advantage of a snowy backdrop and host a cold-weather celebration inspired by an après-ski outing in the mountains. Hot cocktails, fondue and décor with cosy elements you would find at the base of the slopes can help bring this party theme to life.

article_title: A conversation between Bengal’s artistry and Gujarat’s heritage
sub_title: Naina Jain creates a balance of traditional craftsmanship and contemporary elegance with this collection of handcrafted Bandhani sarees
article_content: A lot of different elements take centre stage at Indian weddings—dramatic family members, buffets of delicious food, sangeet performances to popular Bollywood numbers, but, arguably, the bridal outfit steals the show. It’s more than just attire—it’s a canvas of tradition, identity, and artistry. As generations of women adorn themselves in six yards of heritage for their special day, Naina Jain’s collection for the Vogue Wedding Atelier brings together two of India’s rich textile traditions—Bandhani from Gujarat and embroidery from Bengal—in a range of saris designed for women who are both contemporary and in touch with their roots. Renowned for reviving and reimagining Indian textile traditions, Jain’s work celebrates Bandhani—a centuries-old tie-and-dye technique predominantly practiced in western India—with a modern sensibility. Each saree in the collection is meticulously handcrafted by skilled artisans, who tie thousands of minuscule knots into the fabric before dyeing it, resulting in intricate patterns steeped in culture. What truly sets this collection apart is its thoughtful amalgamation of Bandhani with Bengal’s celebrated embroidery techniques, executed by master embroiderers using zardozi, aari, and intricate French knot work. These embellishments exude a delicate opulence, weaving together the visual language of two culturally rich regions into a single, harmonious narrative. The Bengal-inspired embroidery infuses a soft grace into the bold, geometric and organic patterns of Bandhani, striking the perfect balance between structure and fluidity. Floral and animal motifs rendered in detailed embroidery lend an earthy charm to the vivid Bandhani base, transforming each sari into a unique piece of wearable art. The color palette—ranging from jewel-toned maroons and purples to soft pastels and earthy neutrals—further enhances this cross-cultural aesthetic, appealing to both traditional and modern sensibilities. Every sari is more than just a garment; it is an heirloom-in-the-making, symbolising countless hours of labour, intergenerational knowledge, and a deep reverence for India’s diverse textile traditions. Jain’s approach goes beyond fashion; her collection is a celebration of artisanship, sustainability, and regional collaboration. By interweaving Gujarat’s Bandhani, Varanasi’s luxurious weaves, and Bengal’s intricate embroidery, she pays homage not only to technique but also to the communities and stories behind each creation. Whether worn at weddings, festive occasions, or intimate gatherings, these saris resonate with women who cherish authenticity, artistry, and legacy. In an age of fleeting trends, Jain’s collection is a timeless ode to slow, mindful craftsmanship—honoring the past while embracing the elegance of the present.

article_title: How to propose like a pro: Nail these dos and avoid these don’ts
sub_title: Planning to pop the big question? From meaningful locations to post-proposal plans, here are our dos and don’ts for how to propose
article_content: Getting ready to pop the big question, but feeling a bit lost about how to propose? You may have the engagement ring, already tailored to your partner’s ring size and the possibilities for the perfect proposal story swirling in your head. Perhaps you have a few marriage proposal ideas already. A rose-petaled scavenger hunt through your Resist the urge to follow fleeting engagement fads; your wedding proposal deserves to be as one-of-a-kind as your First and foremost, have all the essential conversations about your future with your partner. You want to make sure that marriage is something they are not only open to, but are determined to do. If family is important to your significant other, consider talking to their loved ones to ask permission before getting down on one knee. Surprise proposals are becoming less common, with couples often spending several years together before marriage. According to Put simply, your partner shouldn’t be caught completely off guard by your proposal timing, but the execution is open to personal touches and surprises. In our era of Plan what you want to say beyond the standard, “Will you marry me?” However, it’s best to plan out in bullet points rather than a typed up monologue. You don’t want to sound too robotic or be profusely sweating because you Location matters as well. Choose a spot that holds sentimental value, like you had your first date or where you met during freshman orientation week seven years ago. Speaking of location, it's best to opt for a low-key proposal. Some may love the public display, but emotions can run high and, in general, nobody wants to be proposed to amidst a crowd of tourists, traffic or Mumbai construction—especially if your love is on the timid side. No flash mobs. No busy restaurants. And, absolutely no jumbotrons. (Unless that’s something your partner will love and you’re 100% sure they’ll say yes.) Considering whether to get a photographer document your proposal? Think ahead to ten years from now, when you’ll want to revisit the moment. Or, perhaps the next day when you want to make an engagement announcement on social media. It’s never a bad idea think about hiring a proposal photographer or videographer, or ask a trusted best friend to document the big moment. If this feels impossible to do without spoiling the intimacy, incorporate mementos (like the letter) into the romantic proposal that you can keep or take pictures of afterward. It doesn’t have to be a full-blown photo shoot either. Just capturing the moment can be something that you and the love of your life can cherish forever. Getting down on one knee to propose is a tradition passed down from the medieval era, when knights would do so as a sign of chivalry. Today, the practice continues as a gesture of devotion and reverence to your partner when asking for their hand in marriage. Of course, getting down on one knee is absolutely optional. Just be sure to know for sure if you want to follow the tradition before your proposal takes place. Choose to do it at the last minute and might end up wavering in an awkward semi-lunge. Even if you only practise one time, saying the words you’re planning for your proposal will help you prepare and calm some of those nerves. Rehearse in front of a mirror, to a close friend, or to your pet. You’ll be able to sense how your script flows and what feels most natural to you. Also, remember to practise your physicality—like kneeling or grabbing their left hand to put on the ring. Of course, it doesn’t have to be perfect. Flubbing some words when getting emotional during the real thing will likely be endearing to your partner, rather than a reason for them to say no. If you want to keep an element of surprise for your proposal, it’s best to keep the engagement ring well hidden. That said, you don’t want to lose it either. A loose ring falling through a hole in your pocket onto a sandy beach is the worst-case scenario. Instead, find a secure place where you can stow the ring—preferably in its box—and make sure it’s well concealed. Remember that this is for you, too. Don’t let the stress overwhelm the joy of the occasion—remember, some nerves are good! As the proposer, you have the power to plan something that makes both of you happy. If you’re contemplating a more elaborate or destination proposal, consider hiring a proposal planner to assist with the grandeur of the event. While definitely a splurge, it’s an investment in your well-being if you’re not much of a planner and potentially the rest of your lives. After popping the question, have something special set up to celebrate afterward. You can pop a bottle of champagne, make a reservation at their favourite restaurant, or even set up a small engagement party with friends and family. You’ll absolutely want to savour in the rush after they say ‘yes’ and continue to enjoy in that moment. When your engagement day arrives, the most important thing on your task list to remember is the ring. article_title: Lights, Camera, Say ‘I do’: Embracing the spirit of La Dolce Vita
sub_title: A romantic NYC rooftop proposal, a dreamy Canary Island wedding and a vibrant week-long reverie—Shlok Garg and Revathi Gudi’s love story reads like the most enchanting screenplay—one stitched together by destiny, tradition, and a touch of magic
article_content: Just like any storyteller’s classic true love trope, it was the red string of fate (a theory that connects two individuals who are destined to meet by an invisible red thread) that poetically brought Shlok Garg and Revathi Gudi together. They were the epitome of high school sweethearts. Always in the same space and within each other’s peripheral vision—stealing glances and making do with momentary nods in the high-tension passageways of school. What started as two teens making time for each other between cheerleading and basketball practices, all while planning dates in their hometown of Edison, New Jersey, transformed into something worthwhile in the most unpredictable way. But when life pulled them apart after graduation, love faced its greatest test. Through heartbreak, distance, and life’s many twists, Shlok and Revathi’s connection endured, waiting for the perfect moment to crescendo. They always knew their love story was special—fast forward a few more years, their journey came full circle with a dreamy proposal on a glittering rooftop in New York City, with Manhattan’s skyline unfurling around them and their beloved pet, Mochi, at their feet. The cityscape, the romance, and the candid artistry captured by P.Taufiq Photography turned this private moment into a cinematic prelude for what was to come: a grand wedding celebration, solidified in real, candid frames. The culmination of their love story unfolded in the picturesque landscapes of Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. Amidst the sun-kissed cliffs, lush gardens and the gentle ocean breeze, The Ritz-Carlton, Abama’s Moorish-inspired architecture and unassuming facade made for the ideal canvas for the big day. With the vision of Aria Events weaving every detail and Luxx Escapes curating an impeccable guest experience, Shlok and Revathi's dream destination wedding unfolded like a vibrant tapestry blending South Indian rituals, Punjabi exuberance, and Spanish flair. One breathtaking island, two hundred enthusiastic guests, and a weekend-long reverie were all that was needed to make the celebration perfect. Mochi, of course, made it across the Atlantic Ocean from New Jersey to Spain for the big day, fully embracing each event in coordinating custom outfits made to match the couple. The celebrations kicked off with a vibrant henna ceremony, bathed in rich hues of green. The warm, intimate evening was filled with rhythmic beats of dholki and live folk tunes that made the night crackle with anticipation. The following day welcomed a rustic, Spanish-inspired welcome lunch that set the stage for the wedding weekend and transported guests straight into the heart of Iberian culture. With sun-drenched terraces, vibrant blooms, and culinary delights that paid homage to the island’s heritage, it was a sensorial feast that set the perfect tone for the celebrations to come. Later that evening, the Sangeet unfolded in a whirl of glamour. The venue transformed into a glittering dreamscape of mirrors, crystals, and soaring florals. Spanish flamenco dancers and guitarists from Azúcar intertwined their artistry with high-energy LED performances, while Kunal Lamba curated a dazzling entertainment experience. Platinum Roadshow’s DJ Raj Minocha, kept the dance floor alive into the early hours, weaving a soundscape as electric as the night itself. The second day of festivities began with a haldi ceremony—a fun-filled affair that saw a beautiful setup of vibrant marigold blooms set against the golden hour and the serene waterfront, with every joy-drenched moment documented exquisitely by P.Taufiq Photography. As the wedding day unfolded, the Atlantic Ocean bore witness to a scene straight out of a dream—soft pastel florals framing the sun-kissed altar, violinists serenading the sea breeze with classic Indian melodies, and the horizon igniting as fireworks crowned Shlok and Revathi's vows. At that moment, their love was infinite. For the reception, the couple turned the clock back to the roaring twenties. A Great Gatsby-themed soirée, complete with burlesque singers, flapper dancers, and jazz artists, transported guests into a decadent era of glamour and abandon. The night spilt into an afterparty that spun through the decades into a glittering disco, with each beat and smile captured forever in frames that P.Taufiq Photography so intuitively immortalised. Such is the power of great pictures—they are the ultimate keepsakes for posterity. Reminding us, every once in a while, that maybe everything does happen for a reason.

article_content: In a wholly unique intersection of digital camaraderie and real-world commitment, Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) hosted its first ever in-game wedding—celebrating the union of a couple who first met through the game. What started as an accidental squad addition evolved into a partnership, both in-game and off-screen. Tanupreet considered himself a professional gamer, and he was in no mood to play with a rookie. When a mutual friend added Jaspreet to a game, she was exactly that, still finding her bearings in the game. The story started off with a cliche, the classic enemies to lovers trope playing out. Tanupreet wasn’t particularly thrilled to have to play with Jaspreet. This changed over time and love blossomed. Their squad sessions turned into duo games, where shared tactics and quirks laid the foundation for something deeper. From Jaspreet’s playful map explorations to Tanupreet’s protecting her in the game, their connection blossomed—what began with a parachute drop in Pochinki, a place in the game, culminated in a love story. Blending tradition with technology, BGMI decided to recreate an Indian wedding for this unique couple inside the game, synchronised with their real-world ceremony. The digital festivities mirrored conventional celebrations, including a virtual One of the most important aspects of an Indian wedding are the ensembles. To reflect the ceremonial significance, the bride and groom’s virtual avatars were dressed in custom outfits co-designed by fashion designer Ritu Beri. The garments combined traditional Indian silhouettes with visual cues inspired by BGMI skins, offering a modern yet culturally grounded visual identity for the couple’s in-game avatars. This initiative was part of BGMI’s effort to highlight the real human stories emerging from its digital battlegrounds. “BGMI has been the starting point of so many beautiful relationships. In order to win a match in-game, you have to work together in heightened emotions, so you end up building bonds for a lifetime. Apart from friendships, we've also noticed some lucky couples who met on BGMI and found their life partners. And what better way to celebrate one such lifetime moment than to throw a wedding right inside the game! It's been great fun to see the camaraderie with which our fanbase participated in the grand celebration”, noted Srinjoy Das, associate director of marketing, Krafton India. While BGMI remains known for strategy and survival, stories like this bring into focus a quieter narrative: that the game, for many, is also a space to build relationships, share laughter, and in some cases, find love.

And while the scale of the typical wedding can span the gamut, from an intimate ceremony on a white sandy beach to a mammoth production at a five-star venue, what doesn't change is the attention to detail and cultural personalisation that goes into every element of the big day. Honouring this rich legacy, the Vogue Wedding Atelier presented by HSBC makes its debut in India this August, an invite-only experience bringing together the country's leading bridal couture designers and high jewellery brands, along with experts and bespoke luxury services all under one roof. A sari pavilion, specially curated to celebrate the country's incredible culture of handcrafted textiles from different regions, will feature labels like Dareeab by Sonia K Mahajan, Kanakavalli, Naina Jain and Patola by Nirmal Salvi. Past the diamonds and couture, brides can find space for beauty and skincare with Ajmal, Nexxus New York, Jo Malone London and YSL Beauty.

article_title: How to ace your maid of honour duties—both before and during the wedding
sub_title: Yes, the role comes with some pressure but being asked to be a maid of honour is a sign that you are the bride’s number-one person
article_content: As the leader of the bridal party, there’s no denying that maid of honour duties are an important responsibility. If asked to take on the position, this best friend or close relative of the bride will be in charge of keeping the Yes, the role comes with some pressure—but being asked to be a maid (or man, or person) of honour is an incredible gesture and sign that you are the number-one person that your While the maid of honour’s level of involvement can vary based on how much the The maid of honour is a role designated by the bride as the leader of the bridal party. If the maid of honour is married, you could call them a “matron of honour” instead. Most often, the So what responsibilities fall into the maid of honour’s to-do list before the wedding even takes place? Ahead we break down the key parts of a MOH’s role ahead of the wedding. The most important role of a maid of honour is to be a right hand to the bride. Wedding planning is an exciting time, but it also can occasionally feel like a full-time job. It’s also a period where a couple could be having important The maid of honour is pretty much the camp counsellor of the bridal party. As the leader of the pack, you will ensure everyone is well informed of any and all plans. You will craft group emails and text messages, create itineraries for the bachelorette and wedding day, and answer the necessary questions that the bride doesn’t have to be burdened with. It’s a good idea to collect all wedding party member’s contact info from the bride as soon as you say “yes” to the job so you can get on top of coordination. Be warned that your role as lead communicator might have to come down to working out any conflicts within the group as well. The bachelorette party is likely the biggest undertaking a maid of honour will take. If the bride decides to do a destination trip, you will likely be charged with securing a hotel or Airbnb, organising activities, making reservations, creating a budget and getting payments from the attendees. Throughout the event, you should play check-in frequently to make sure the plans are running smoothly and the bride is having a great time. While you might be the leader of the event, it’s totally fine (and encouraged for your own wellbeing) to delegate and collaborate with other bridal party members to bring plans to life. Traditionally, the maid of honour would also take charge of planning the bridal shower. Today, that isn’t necessarily the case. While a MOH can still host the bridal shower, a close family member or multiple people in the bridal party may offer to plan the event, too. This party is all about “showering” a bride with gifts while surrounded by close friends and female family members. If you are hosting, it’s important to find a great venue, send invitations, supply food and drinks, curate decorations and organise fun activities for the guests. You also should help lead the gift-giving part of the event and keep the list of presents organised so the bride can easily write thank-you notes later. Once the bride decides their vision for the wedding party attire, the maid of honour should help to make sure the bridal party all gets appropriate looks. Many wedding parties don’t all wear the exact same dress anymore, so it’s a good idea to work with the bride to send an email with all the details of outfit guidelines, providing timelines needed for orders or approvals, and follow up to ensure everyone has their ensembles ready in time for the big day. Once the wedding day arrives, a maid of honour will need to kick into high gear to take on these important tasks. There are lots of moving parts on a wedding day, from getting hair and makeup done to taking photos to walking down the aisle. A maid of honour should be there to help corral the bridal party to make it to every event in a timely manner. The morning of a wedding can be a fun and meaningful time for the bridal party as they all get ready for the big day. The maid of honour should make sure this space is well prepared with food, water, and maybe a little champagne for everyone to enjoy as they get glammed up and prepare for the long day ahead. The bride should have a relaxing wedding day—and not be the person fielding questions from a wedding planner or confused guests. The maid of honour will help with those last coordinating details and relay any necessary information to the wedding party. It’s a good idea to get contact info of the wedding planners or venue coordinators before the day of so you can be in communication at all times. It’s perfectly normal for a bride who’s distracted by all the moving parts to forget about eating enough during the day or get some jitters. A maid of honour should be on top of ensuring the bride always has food and water available, as well as being a shoulder for them to lean on if they need to talk through any nerves. During the ceremony, a bride will traditionally hand off the bouquet to the maid of honour for important moments like vows and exchanging rings. In addition to the floral arrangement, a maid of honour may be asked to hold onto items for the bride like lipstick, a cell phone, or a speech. It’s a good idea to keep a clutch with you or choose an outfit with pockets for this purpose. You might also need to join the bride in the bathroom if their large lehenga needs to be strategically held when they’re relieving themselves. At the reception, you might also be needed to take the gift envelopes received by the couple to a place for safekeeping. Traditionally, the maid of honour is one of the few guests who give a speech at the wedding reception. It’s best to make this speech sweet, sentimental, and a bit funny, if that’s your forté. Make sure to pre-write your speech and practise if you can so you don’t let nerves take hold. Also, be sure to keep it on the shorter side so everyone can have plenty of time later on the dance floor. While you absolutely can enjoy the specialty cocktails and get down on the dance floor, it’s best for the maid of honour not to go overboard. Feel free to keep your energy up and have fun alongside the bride all night, but remember that you should still be a helpful presence rather than someone who needs help. If there’s a day-after party, you will want to be in good shape to help the bride with any last needs.

article_title: This Toronto-based couple celebrated their multicultural wedding in vibrant Goa
sub_title: Nick and Priya’s sunset nuptials were a nod to their fun, outgoing personalities, paired with a dose of surreal views at Hilton Goa
article_content: Some love stories unfold quietly, but with an ease that makes them feel destined. For Nick Alexander and Priya Bandodkar, that moment began during a college meet-and-greet in Canada, when Priya first noticed Nick flailing enthusiastically through a virtual reality demo. “He later told me he’d planned the whole thing—to make an impression on the new students,” she laughs. That playful energy never left their relationship. Over the years, the two grew closer, finding comfort and companionship in one another. “We spent a lot of time together during the lockdowns, and the day we brought our dog Toby home was the moment we both felt like a real family,” Priya recalls. Their journey took a romantic turn in Venice when Nick proposed on a gondola under the famous Bridge of Lovers. “The legend says a kiss beneath it ensures eternal love—he timed it perfectly.” When it came to planning their wedding, there was never a doubt it would take place in India. “We wanted Nick’s family to truly experience the culture I grew up with,” says Priya. “But more than that, it was about creating a space where two very different families could meet, bond, and make memories together.” After scouting a few venues, the couple found exactly what they were looking for at Hilton Goa Resort, nestled above the Nerul River. “It just felt different. The views from the highest terrace took our breath away. We looked at each other and instantly knew—we’re getting married here, at sunset,” she says. The resort’s peaceful surroundings, sweeping terraces, and proximity to Candolim and Panjim meant their guests could enjoy a full Goan experience, from celebration to sightseeing. Their wedding weekend unfolded with a joyful The reception brought a dose of modern glamour, as the couple and their guests celebrated late into the night, soaking up every last moment. Beyond the beautiful rituals, the couple made a conscious effort to include sustainable and local touches that reflected their values. “At the Planning a wedding from across the world can be a challenge—but the Hilton team made it feel seamless. “We visited once before finalising the venue, but after that, everything happened remotely,” she explains. “The hotel team, and especially our Hilton Wedding Ambassador, made sure we felt supported at every stage. It was like having someone on the ground who genuinely understood what we wanted and made it happen.” In the end, their wedding wasn’t just a celebration of their love—but of cultures coming together, families finding common ground, and memories being made in a place that now holds a very special spot in their hearts.

article_title: Inside a Jaipur couple’s grand wedding in Rajasthan’s Aravalli Hills
sub_title: Arpit and Khushboo’s wedding ceremony at DoubleTree by Hilton Jaipur Amer blended their love story with immersive experiences for guests
article_content: For Arpit Parwal and Khushboo Choraria, love first sparked in the corridors of their high school in Jaipur. What started as a teenage friendship turned into a lifelong bond, one that endured distance, time zones, and countless video calls. “On Valentine’s Day in 10th grade, Khushboo got down on one knee in the middle of the school grounds and asked me to be her Valentine,” Arpit recalls. “That moment set the course for everything that followed.” Even as life (and their careers) initially took them to different cities, Arpit works as a software engineer in Seattle, USA, while Khushboo has now launched her own custom gifting and jewellery brand, their connection remained unbreakable. “Despite the miles, we always found our way back to each other,” they share. So, when it came to their wedding, they knew it had to be a celebration of their story—a blend of grand gestures and intimate, thoughtful details. For the Jaipur natives, a local wedding venue that still felt like a destination was key. “We wanted something scenic, luxurious, and easily accessible for our guests,” Khushboo explains. DoubleTree by Hilton Jaipur Amer, nestled against the Aravalli Hills, offered the perfect mix of breathtaking views and seamless hospitality. “Beyond the stunning location, it was Hilton’s expertise in hosting large-scale weddings that sealed the deal,” Arpit shares. The hotel’s Wedding Ambassador worked closely with us from day one, helping us craft a stress-free experience that allowed us to focus on enjoying our celebrations. For Arpit and Khushboo, their wedding wasn’t just about them—it was about making their family and friends feel truly special and welcomed. Thoughtful gestures were incorporated right from the time guests arrived, until their departure. For instance, welcome hampers were stocked with the couple’s favourite snacks with personal notes explaining why each item was chosen. A custom radio show played in cars that ferried guests from the airport, sharing stories about the couple’s journey, while room keys were handed in the form of a ‘Book of Love’, that doubled as a keepsake, complete with the wedding itinerary and tiny, personalised elements. Another feature that was a hit with guests was a live wedding magazine updated via their Instagram handle, that ensured guests felt part of the journey, weeks before the celebrations began. “Hilton’s Wedding Ambassador made sure every touchpoint was executed perfectly,” Khushboo shares. “From coordinating the guest arrivals to handling last-minute changes, they were our support system.” Each event was themed around a chapter of their love story. So, the welcome party was themed as an ‘Around the World’ carnival—a nod to their shared love for travel, featuring favourite dishes from places they visited together. The after-party was inspired by an airport lounge, thanks to the years of long-distance travel that the couple undertook, along with personalised boarding pass invitations. Menus were tailored for each event, from an authentic Rajasthani feast at the bhaat ceremony to a global gourmet spread reflecting their travels. "We worked closely with Hilton’s F&B team to ensure every dish felt intentional," Arpit adds. One of the most emotional moments came during the sangeet, as the couple exchanged rings while over 40 of their closest friends cheered them on. “Seeing that love and support from our people, it was overwhelming in the best way,” Arpit recalls. As the wedding celebrations unfolded under the Jaipur night sky, guests were treated to a spectacular sufi performance, fireworks, and an evening of dance and revelry. “Thanks to Hilton’s Wedding Ambassador and the team, we were able to fully immerse ourselves in the joy of our wedding, without worrying about a thing.” For the couple, their wedding was a celebration of their story, their journey, and the people who made it special. "As the sky turned an inky blue and we toasted to our new life together, we knew one thing for sure—this was exactly how we had imagined it," they share.

article_title: A confluence of innovation and creativity
sub_title: From selecting the ideal location to managing all other aspects of a wedding, Shloka Events is helping couples and families alike to navigate the logistics of wedding planning
article_content: Weddings in India are more than just a union of two individuals—they are a vibrant celebration of culture, tradition, and families coming together. From choosing the perfect venue, orchestrating intricate ceremonies and ensuring guests are taken care of, wedding planning is both an art and a science which will have one juggling the tasks of ten people. With wedding planning becoming one of the fastest-growing sectors in India, planners are now devoted to handling everything, from destinations to decor. Enter Shloka Events, a company specialising in end-to-end event solutions for social and corporate events. Since its inception in 2014, Shloka Events has combined creativity and professionalism to curate a unique wedding experience for everyone. Boasting a curation of lavish weddings in locations like Istanbul, Doha, Bali and Udaipur, the company is breaking away from convention to create contemporary and chic experiences. article_title: The Hilton Expert Series: Documenting love stories behind the lens one frame at a time
sub_title: Arjun Kartha, founder of Twogether Studios and Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador, share expert tips for couples for capturing those precious wedding memories on film
article_content: Weddings are a magical blend of love, laughter, memories and shared traditions. From the time you gather with your family and friends, walk down the aisle and share stolen glances with your significant other, to toasting to a lifetime together—all combined in a vibrant celebration—it’s these little moments that make any wedding a standout affair. And it’s only fitting that these precious moments be captured on camera so you can look back on them fondly, no matter how much time has passed by. However, finding the right photography team or studio for your dream wedding is easier said than done. You want to be able to work with a team that understands your vision, who you are as a couple, and the kind of photography you’re both looking for— whether moody, cinematic, editorial or taking the much-loved storytelling approach. Arjun Kartha, founder of Delhi-based Twogether Studios which has been a leading name in wedding photography and cinematography for the past decade, and Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador, take us through According to Kartha, one of the key factors to pulling off a dream wedding is setting aside enough time to capture moments on film. Couples often tend to overlook this small but significant step that allows them to capture those fleeting but heartwarming moments. “Instead of squeezing multiple events into a single day, consider spacing them out, so the team has enough room to capture those meaningful moments—like your couple portraits, family group shots and candid interactions—without feeling too rushed,” he suggests. Kartha can’t emphasise enough on the importance of sketching out a brief for your photography studio. How about putting together a mood board for them to reference? According to him, this kind of visual inspiration is invaluable. “For example, Pinterest boards are a great way to convey this,” he explains, adding that this helps the photographer to understand your aesthetic and preferences—whether you’re drawn to soft, pastel hues, bold pops of color, sleek modern lines, or even classic, timeless looks. He cautions that it’s also important to keep your expectations realistic. “For instance, if you’re having a night wedding, your inspiration shouldn’t be drawn from daytime functions.” Equally important is clarity around what you don’t want, he adds. “Lean into what your vibe is as a couple and allow that to be front and centre of your story,” suggests Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador. Personalisation is key here, as you can add several tiny details to your wedding celebrations that will reflect your story and journey. She recalls working with a bride recently who wanted to embroider her husband’s name onto her wedding saree, making for a heartfelt keepsake. According to Kaur, what matters beyond curating the perfect decor, a great food spread and the right dose of entertainment, is crafting meaningful moments that reflect your story, which will ultimately translate on film. This could be anything from personalising your wedding ceremony set-up that is unique to your family’s traditions or focusing on who you both are by bringing your own ideas and thoughts to the table. “Share as many details and ideas that you have in mind, and we’ll work towards making it happen,” she says. Kaur adds that as wedding ambassadors, the team and the hotel are always available at hand to help couples with the best photo-friendly locations, capture the perfect shot for the gram, and even work behind the scenes with the photographers to ensure its smooth sailing on your big day. While trends in the wedding space can be fleeting, they can also work in elevating your wedding photos and film. Kartha believes that storytelling and authenticity are definitely at the forefront of wedding photography at the moment. “Couples increasingly want their images to feel like a true reflection of who they are, rather than a series of staged moments. This means focusing on interactions, raw emotions, and capturing the atmosphere and energy of the celebration as it naturally unfolds.” This also allows wedding photography to serve both as art and memory—with gorgeous, evocative imagery that showcases the couple’s story.

article_title: Why this couple chose a magical riverfront wedding at DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji over the beach
sub_title: Tanya Sharma and Tarun Makhijani tied the knot in a colourful celebration overlooking the Mandovi River in Panaji, Goa
article_content: Most couples who choose Goa for a destination wedding, do so with the expectation of having a scenic beachfront wedding, complete with sunset pheras and fireworks thrown in for good measure. Tanya Sharma and Tarun Makhijani decided otherwise, choosing to skip the classic beach wedding for a quaint riverfront setting at the DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji. Goa held a special place in their heart—it’s where their love story began, as Tarun, a well-known wedding and club DJ, and Tanya first met at a celebration there. “We were introduced by common friends and spoke briefly. We didn’t think much of it, carrying on with our lives. It was only in 2020 during the lockdown when he reached out via text and we started talking,” Sharma reveals. Their worlds might have been far apart—Tanya works as an independent sports consultant, while Tarun is a wedding and club DJ—however fate had its way and four years later, they decided to seal their love in a surreal celebration surrounded by their closest family and friends—back where it all began. The couple knew they wanted to host their nuptials in Goa, but a beach wedding wasn’t on the cards. Instead, they started looking for one-off venues that retained Goa’s charm and offered a different take on the sunshine state. A visit to the DoubleTree by Hilton Goa- Panaji, ticked all the boxes for the couple and their families, with its quaint location in the capital city, scenic river views and distant hills framing the backdrop. DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji offers breathtaking vistas of lush hills and winding waters, paired with modern luxury across its 160 elegant rooms and suites. Nestled on the banks of the winding Mandovi River with 160 rooms and suites, the resort offers unparalleled vistas set in the lap of nature. “We loved the fact that the resort had this gorgeous setting overlooking the river and the hills, and enough venue options for each of our celebrations,” they both share. The celebrations began with an intimate haldi ceremony in the alfresco area of a charming riverside restaurant, with vibrant marigold decor. This was followed by the mehendi in the bride’s suite clubbed with a private terrace. The next day, the infinity pool became the perfect venue for a lively sundowner featuring craft cocktails and fun games—an ideal setting to capture those gram-worthy shots and soak up the pleasant weather. Unbeknownst to Sharma, her beau had a surprise proposal planned for her at the pool party, where he went down on one knee and slipped a sparkling diamond ring on her finger, with their friends and family cheering them on. “Somehow, he managed to rope in our closest friends to pull off this surprise and sweep me off my feet,” Tanya reveals. The evening’s revelry continued with a grand sangeet and cocktail party in the resort’s expansive ballroom, known for its elegant design and ability to host lively celebrations. The couple were treated to special dance performances by their friends and family, as well as a live band that belted out several hits. The next day dawned bright and early with perfect weather, as the resort’s poolside venue underwent a transformation for the set-up of the wedding mandap. For Tanya, one of the most precious memories from their special day was when she walked down the aisle towards her beau. “I loved everything about my bridal entry. The fact that Tarun was in tears when he first saw me as a bride, was both emotional and beautiful at the same time,” she shares. As they took their pheras, with a dramatic sunset for company that painted the sky in vibrant hues, the love in the air was palpable. This was followed by a live sufi act and fireworks for a fitting finale. The celebrations ended with a reception and dinner in the ballroom with a curated F&B set-up for their guests to relish. “Every detail was thoughtfully curated, from my bridal entry to the custom menu. The team worked closely with us to infuse personal touches, like late-night snacks tailored for our post-dance cravings,” Tanya shares. “The F&B team ensured everything reflected our tastes, from indulgent local Goan dishes to a curated dessert station with our favourite treats,” they added, referring to how the hotel’s chefs personally sat down with them to curate menus, all the way from breakfast to midnight munchies, especially after the long nights of dancing and revelry. “Everything was planned with so much detail and love, and what made it all the more special was seeing our family and friends have such a fabulous time at our wedding,” they add. As the sky turned an inky blue, washing away the vibrant sunset hues, the couple toasted with glasses of champagne to a brand-new chapter in their lives, marking the perfect finale to their wedding celebrations.

article_title: How to write and deliver the best wedding speech
sub_title: Whether you’re the father of the bride, best man, or maid of honour, learn how to write—and deliver—the best wedding speech
article_content: If one of your nearest and dearest is tying the knot, it’s possible you may feel pressured to deliver the best A wedding speech presents a unique challenge: There’s no set formula for how the speech should play out, but it often requires sentimentality, a touch of humour and the good sense to know when to wrap it up. That’s why it’s pretty easy to overthink how Have you been asked to give a wedding toast at an upcoming celebration? There’s no reason to sweat. Instead, read ahead to learn how to write the best wedding speech and plan for your big moment. First off, it’s important to make sure that the couple definitely The to-be-weds also have the right to curate the day as they wish, and occasionally at a rehearsal dinner or welcome party, the couple may open the floor to additional toasts. But if this doesn’t happen, grabbing the mic unexpectedly for an off-the-cuff speech (especially after a few glasses of wine) will not be appreciated. If you are asked to give a toast, it’s important that you don’t just wing it. “First, recognise that speechwriting is a creative process,” shares Allison Shapira, founder and CEO of Global Public Speaking. “Give yourself plenty of time to be creative (i.e. not the night before, when you already have so much to stress about). Wait for your most creative time of the day, and turn off any distractions. Spend some unrushed time thinking about your relationship to the couple, and what you’d like to say.” While there’s no exact template to follow, there is a common basic formula to adhere to. “The framework I recommend for a wedding speech is: story, message, blessing,” Shapira shares. “Tell a heartwarming story, share the message or value behind that story, and then offer a blessing or wish for the couple based on that message.” “Typically, we advise our speakers to try to bring the audience on a journey where you initially try to make them laugh, then get to the real depth of the speech and earn some tears, then bring the whole speech full circle with a deep insight or story about the couple that ends with a funny final punch,” says Steven Greitzer, CEO and founder of Provenance, an AI company that specialises in helping write personalised wedding vows, ceremonies, and toasts. “It’s important to have a good balance of humour and sentimentality because, if it’s a full roast, it can feel like you’re just doing a standup comedy show for your own benefit and it could lack substance. Or, if it’s too overly emotional, it can get heavy and perhaps a bit too somber for a wedding celebration.” When choosing a story, Shapira recommends thinking carefully about who will be in the room. “It should obviously be good-natured, without making anyone look bad. And, it all depends on the family dynamics,” she says. “What one family considers good-natured, another family could consider scathing. Choose someone in the audience whom you think could give you some helpful feedback, and practise the speech with them in advance.” Greitzer adds that it’s important for both members of the couple to be highlighted in the speech. “Great anecdotes showcase who each person was before meeting, their synergy together, and their individual and collective growth,” he says. If you don’t know one member of the happy couple very well and are unfamiliar with their love story, don’t be afraid to get creative. “One of the best speeches I’ve seen was from a bridesmaid who hadn’t really been able to spend too much time with her best friend’s fiance because of the pandemic,” Greitzer shares. “She creatively read texts she found in her phone that gave her a hilarious timeline of her friend falling in love.” If you’re still not sure where to begin, consider giving an AI platform a try to help you form your toast. “The Provenance tools guide speakers to create unique, and personal ceremonies, vows, and toasts without the stress. It’s a partner in your brainstorming process; a way to help you verbalise what you were trying to say—but faster,” explains Greitzer. “Instead of being some outdated, mad-libs-style template, the expert-curated prompts inspire special stories and insights, ultimately weaving your responses together into a custom, editable first draft.” A final writing tip from Shapira? “I definitely recommend creating an outline but do not recommend writing the speech out word for word. When we script the entire speech, it sounds too formal,” says the public speaking expert. “I recommend first brainstorming the content, rearranging it into a logical structure, then drafting a general outline which you can bring with you to the event. While it may look better to simply give the speech ‘from the heart,’ the stress involved in trying to memorise your speech is simply not worth it.” The ideal length of a toast is between two to four minutes, which translates to around 500 to 1000 words on a page. Still, Greitzer notes, “The perfect length for the wedding toast complies with whatever length the couple wants it to be. Many guests don’t realise that long speeches can impact the whole evening’s timeline and affect the caterer, DJ, and so much more.” Best rule of thumb? Keep it short and sweet. Writing a wedding speech is half the battle—next comes your performance. It’s important that your toast has a good flow, feels natural, and doesn’t drag on. Here’s where the idiom “practice makes perfect” rings true. Shapira advises giving yourself a few weeks of rehearsal to make your speech feel authentic and fluid. Her recommendations? “Read your speech out loud and make sure it stays within the time you have allotted. Read it to someone else and get their feedback. Record it and watch it back. We use a tool called AMPLIFY to get AI-based feedback.” She adds, “Don’t memorise the speech, but do read it out loud and make sure it sounds like your voice.” While it’s now common to see toasts being read off a phone, both experts agree that it’s much better to print out your speech. “Reading off of a phone comes with the risk of distractions from notifications, a weird backlight that can affect the colour of your face in photos, finicky technical difficulties, and having that annoying sound interference with the mic,” says Greitzer. (You also should make sure your speech is legible with a large font and wide spacing so you can easily find your place.) Watching yourself in front of a mirror can also be helpful to understand your body language during the performance. The final hurdle of giving a wedding toast is getting over your nerves. “Find a quiet place right beforehand to centre yourself (perhaps the bathroom or a corner of the room), pause and breathe, and remind yourself why you care about the couple,” recommends Shapira. She also adds—perhaps unsurprisingly—that it’s best to hold back on alcohol consumption ahead of the toast. You might think liquid courage can help you, but it’s best to not let yourself go a glass too far. “No one expects a perfect or professional speech; they want a unique, authentic message. The speech isn’t about you—it’s about the couple. Once you reframe the fact that the centre of attention isn’t on you, you can relax.”

article_title: How to say no to being a bridesmaid? It’s easier than you think

article_content: If you’ve ever wondered how to say no to being a “I think one of the hard and fast rules is when this question gets asked of you is to ask about what the role entails. You can even say to someone, ‘Oh my gosh, from a totally emotional point, yes, I’m there 100 per cent. But tell me what the actual logistics are and the expectations that you have, because it’s your day and you should really have a group of people that can meet that “Personally, I think it’s okay to decline being a part of someone’s wedding as long as you have a real-life, legitimate excuse,” says editor and former Moda Operandi communications director Hayley Bloomingdale, who’s been in such delicate situations herself. “If you genuinely can’t make it to the actual nuptials, then obviously, the Still, it’s tough to be in the position of turning down a hopeful bride. And, what if you’re approached to take on a role that needs to take on more responsibility like a maid of honour? Here, wedding experts offer tips on how to say no to being a bridesmaid (and still be a good friend). If imagining serving as a bridesmaid gives you When it comes to matrimonial commitments, financial transparency is key, says event and wedding planner Brianne Garritano, adding that weddings, and the cost of being a bridesmaid, are more complex nowadays. According to a study by If being a bridesmaid is outside of your current financial budget, you don’t have to go into debt just because you were asked. “It can be really, really hard,” shares Post. “You feel like you’re letting someone down, and yet at the same time, it’s their event, it’s not your event. They’re doing it on their budget and their scale and with their requirements to fit their dream—it’s okay if you can’t actually participate in that. Even though often people think it’s not polite to talk about money, this is an instance where letting someone know that the budget is prohibitive for you is an important one.” She adds being upfront about not being able to take time off work is another very valid reason for bowing out of festivities. If you’re worried about the financial and time commitment of pre-wedding events for the bridal party, Post reveals an etiquette rule that many might not know. “Bridesmaids are not required to go to any of those events—bachelorette party, showers, anything,” she shares. “What they are required to do is show up for the rehearsal, the ceremony and the reception. Typically, you would think they’d be required as long as their travel schedule allows them to attend something like a bridesmaid’s luncheon because it is being thrown for them. But nobody Speaking of taking the lead, serving as the maid of honour is a time-consuming role that’s not to be taken lightly. And if you’re in the unenviable position of having to decline the position, don’t waste any time telling the bride. “You should tell her right away, as soon as possible,” says event and wedding planner Mindy Weiss, adding that the conversation should take place in person when possible, and over the phone if not. The key is to have it as soon as you can. “The longer you wait, the more difficult it is on yourself and the bride. So as soon as you have an inkling that you may not be able to make the commitment, you should let her know. Don’t leave her in a bind; don’t put shock value on it. The sooner the better." Also, watch the impulse to feel defensive—even if the invite puts you on the spot or makes you feel uncomfortable. “Don’t be angry,” Weiss says. “Just be gentle, be honest, and talk about it. There could be financial reasons you can’t participate, or it could be that you don’t have enough time to do it and you don’t want to disappoint. Explain that gently, and the bride will understand.” Feel like you aren’t the kind of organisational leader to take on the tasks required of a maid of honour? You’re allowed to bow out or ask to just be a regular bridal party member. Post shares, “It is okay to just say, even without budget or time being a reason, ‘I am so honoured by the offer, but this is not a role that I feel good playing and it’s nothing to do with our relationship. I love you. I support you. I am so excited to go to your wedding and I’m really happy for you. But please don’t ask me to be that.’” She adds, “A lot of us know when we have a friend who this will be torture for. You know what I mean? Give her the break. Ask your cousin instead.”
